features.name: Shared WhatsApp inbox

invariants.rule: Closing a lead records a structured reason and optional note, Other requires an explanation, closed reasons remain searchable, and a new customer reply reopens the conversation and clears the closure details.
Buyer-alert onboarding assumes Buying when intent is unstated, persists that default, proceeds directly to sale budget bands, and offers Renting instead as an explicit exception.

Buyer locations accept Bengaluru real-estate market zones (CBD & Off-CBD, SBD, ORR and PBD East/South/North) plus directional zones, normalize Bangalore and Bengaluru spellings, and match inventory in member localities without leaking into unrelated zones.

A buyer's stated locality matches inventory across spelling variants, listings in that locality lead every buyer-facing shortlist ordered by property-type fit before nearby listings, a stated plot type ranks plot listings above houses, and a locality the buyer types is saved in the spelling they typed (or the curated locality) rather than a misspelt inventory variant.

A single stated plot size admits larger plots up to 35% over as near-fits ranked below exact fits and within-10% near-misses, including when a full brief clamps their scores; smaller plots and plots beyond that headroom are excluded, and a stated size band keeps its strict cap.

A lead asking for more listings receives the next matches the share ledger says they have not seen, with nothing filed and no question asked; the qualification ladder never asks a rung twice in a thread; relative size feedback never stores a floor above the cap it cleared.

The latest outbound sender owns qualification replies: a later agent message keeps the bot quiet, while a later bot message resumes automation so an older agent message cannot leave a fresh buyer requirement unanswered.

A Meta error that blocks Marketing to one recipient — the frequency cap 131049 and the experiment block 130472 — never changes the composed message body: it records structured failure metadata under Meta's own code, pauses only Marketing templates for that contact (at least 24 hours for the cap, a 30-day horizon for the experiment), defers queued alerts without consuming retries, clears the pause when the contact replies, and gives web and mobile agents a friendly status naming the cause with no immediate resend action; Utility templates remain eligible. Only a verdict from Meta sets a pause: the dispatcher and the status webhook each keep whichever standing pause runs longer, and a send the local guard itself refused never extends one, so retries cannot hold a pause open indefinitely.

A lead who taps "Close my enquiry" on a check-in or enquiry template is asked, after the acknowledgement, why the shared property did not fit: the property is resolved from the quoted template, the last week of outbound messages or the recorded enquiry; the one-tap reason (budget, location, type, size, bought elsewhere, not buying now, other) is filed on listing feedback, the contact timeline and the active journey item, the agent is notified, both messages bypass the dead-contact gate, and the question never promises to be the last message.

"Close my enquiry" closes the enquiry on the listing the template named, not the lead: that listing is rejected for the contact and its journey branch dropped, the contact stays live, matching and on whatever alert consent they last gave, and the acknowledgement says their other enquiries stay open. After the drop-off reason (or at once when the close names no listing) the lead is shown their open enquiries (active journey branches not already at a closing or won stage) as a one-tap list — close any of them, or keep them all, each answer logged on the journey — and then the requirement ladder or their current matches; "bought elsewhere" and "not buying right now" instead park the search by marking the contact dead, and the drop-off reason is filed on the branch the close already dropped. Only a close that names no listing on a journey with nothing open marks the contact dead, and START ALERTS in the lead's own words revives a dead contact, un-parks the requirement and grants consent before the confirmation and ladder go out.

❄️ Mark cold on a follow-up radar card closes the enquiry on the listing the card named, not the lead: that listing is rejected and its journey branch dropped for every member of the party, and the lead stays HOT while any other enquiry (an active journey branch not at a closing or won stage) is still open, with the lead's last enquired listing moved onto one of those so the next card names it; the agent is told which enquiries are still tracked. Only when that listing was the last open enquiry, or the card named no listing, does the lead go COLD; the last check for an open enquiry and the COLD update run as one locked database step (mark_party_cold_unless_open, with every branch that becomes active or changes stage taking the same contact lock, and a stage rewrite waiting on it), so an enquiry that lands first keeps the lead hot instead of racing the cold. A card whose listing can no longer be read (deleted, or the lookup failed), whose party's open enquiries cannot be read, or which was sent before cards named their listing, leaves the lead as it is and says so, rather than falling back to a lead-wide cold. A close whose feedback or journey write failed, or that left the carded branch active, keeps the lead's temperature and tells the agent the close did not finish and may be partial; a COLD update that fails or changes no lead, is never confirmed as done; when the close succeeded but moving the lead onto its remaining enquiry failed, the agent is told the listing was closed and the lead could not be moved. A card carries a listing in its Mark cold action only when it names that listing; a card whose listing exists but could not be named offers no Mark cold at all, so neither a hidden listing nor a lead-wide cold can come from it.

A funnel keyword buried in a lead’s text question never restarts a flow that lead has already been through: once a listing has been sent to them, or they ask for a person, the matched flow is skipped and the question is answered from that listing instead. Asking for a person counts whether typed or tapped: a template quick reply whose label asks for a person ("Talk to someone", "Call me back") gets the same callback promise, agent notification, bridged relay and pending flag as a typed "call me". Any other quick-reply label is never read as a question. A tap is matched against flow keywords by its raw label, never the inbox's decorated rendering, so an exact-match flow keyed on a label opens on that tap. A flow they have never entered still opens on its own keyword, and a lead who has been sent nothing is still qualified by the funnel. Entry only — an active run still advances.

tests.case: [INB-011] reads a quick-reply tap asking for a person as a callback request
does not restart a flow on a quick-reply tap that asks for a person
opens an exact-match flow keyed on the tapped label

invariants.rule: The shipped showcase funnel enters on openers and explicit intent phrases only, never on a bare word a property conversation is made of. The flow builder warns, without blocking activation, when a contains-matched entry keyword is such a word, and no shipped template trips that warning. A showcase flow still carrying a stock keyword list is moved to the tightened one; an edited list is left alone.

An inbox attachment is staged straight into the account's own chat-media prefix under a server-signed, single-path upload URL rather than through the app, so the caps the composer advertises (5 MB image, 16 MB video, 100 MB document) are the caps that apply; web and mobile refuse an unsupported type or an oversized file in the same words before uploading, and a media send reads the staged object back and refuses one that is missing, outside the account, or larger than Meta's cap before handing the link to Meta.

The qualification ladder never drops or re-asks what a lead already said: a bare size ("1200 sqft", "30x40") is filed as a requirement, lines of one burst are filed together and in order whatever order their webhooks land in, one conversation is qualified by one webhook at a time under the inbound chain's conversation lease (INB-016), never a second lease of its own (same-second lines are ordered by their ingestion sequence), buy-or-rent follows the newest line of the burst that states it (a bare "Rent" correcting "Buy" included) so no older webhook undoes a newer one, and a budget no rent could reach (₹10 L+, ₹1 Cr+ for commercial) answers buy-or-rent. A lead who asks for matches when nothing fits is told what was searched and asked the next missing rung, never told to change a brief they never gave.

When nothing fits a lead's brief but their own locality has live listings of the same deal type at another price or type, the no-match reply (the requirement playback card and the on-demand matches reply) names how many, their price band (monthly rent for rentals, as the matching engine prices them; one deal type per band, with untyped listings read as Sale) and, only when the lead's budget is on the same basis, whether it is above or below it, with a link scoped to those listings; when there are more than the link carries, the reply says the link shows the ones closest to the budget (or the most affordable) and a scan that hits its bound is stated as "N+". Housing-board prefixes such as "KHB" never stop a locality from matching.

Every automated handler for an inbound WhatsApp message (control replies, the owner chatbot, update sessions, qualification, flows, lead Q&A and automations) runs for one conversation one message at a time under a single conversation lease taken after the message is stored, so overlapping webhooks never start two flow runs, advance a flow step twice, or double-send a condition-guarded automation, and only the earliest of racing first messages fires first_inbound_message. A run that waited reads the contact and conversation afresh. A webhook that cannot get the lease in time hands the holder its whole handler context (never the access token), and the holder reruns the full chain for it exactly once; a deferred id with no stored context is only qualified, and a live lease that cannot take the message logs and skips the handlers rather than running them unlocked. A claim that still errors after three short retries (about two seconds), or a missing service-role client, is treated as that same busy case: nothing runs unlocked. A holder never deletes a lease that may carry deferred ids: when it hits its deferred-rounds cap or its finish fails it lets the lease expire, and the next holder of the conversation runs what was left after its own message and clears each payload as it takes it. Different conversations run in parallel.

A cron resume of a waiting automation runs exactly once and never inside an inbound chain: each due automation_pending_executions row is claimed atomically under a claim token before it runs (overlapping cron runs split the rows, never share one), and only that claim settles it as done or failed. The resume runs under the same conversation lease as INB-016 (the row's conversation, else the contact's thread), never waits for it: a live lease, or a lease claim that stays indeterminate, releases the claim and leaves the row pending for the next tick without spending an attempt. The resume holds the lease for at most about 20 seconds, shorter than an inbound waiter's 30, so an inbound message is not deferred to it, and it never runs deferred inbound ids: it lets the lease expire with them for the next inbound holder. A row stuck running past 15 minutes is reclaimed, and after 3 attempts it is marked failed. Immediately before it executes, a resume re-asserts its claim token (refreshing claimed_at) and skips a row another run has reclaimed. Each row looks up its contact's conversation immediately before it runs, not when the batch is claimed, so a conversation created meanwhile is leased; a conversation stored on the row that no longer exists is replaced, for both the lease and the resumed steps' sends, by the contact's current thread (or dropped when there is none) rather than retried forever; a failed lookup, one still unanswered when the time budget ends, or one that answers only after it has ended, releases the claim rather than running, and never holds up another conversation's rows. Only a contact with no conversation at that moment, or no contact, runs unlocked, since there is nothing to serialise against. A batch runs up to five conversations at once, each conversation's rows one at a time in run_at order, so a slow resume never holds up another conversation; automation webhooks time out after 10 seconds, and rows not started within the route's time budget are released back to pending.

A post-call outreach follow-up and a property-share feedback request each go out once and never inside an inbound chain. Each is claimed before it sends (a follow-up by moving its scheduled_for 15 minutes ahead while it stays pending, a share by stamping feedback_sent_at while it stays pending), so overlapping runs never send the same one twice, and a claim left by a run that died is taken over after 15 minutes (a claimed share stays eligible 30 minutes past the two-hour send window so that takeover can happen). The send then runs under the same conversation lease as INB-016 for the lead's thread and re-reads the thread under it: the window for a follow-up, and whether the buyer has replied since the share for a feedback request. Sweeps never wait for the lease; the voice webhook's immediate follow-up waits up to 20 seconds. A busy conversation, a failed conversation lookup, or a failed window check releases the claim without sending: the follow-up becomes due for the next sweep (an immediate one included) and the share is retried on the next run. A share whose send Meta refuses is released rather than marked sent. Only a lead with no conversation sends without a lease.

The flows cron times out a stale active flow run only under the same conversation lease as INB-016 for the run's contact, never waiting for it, and only if the run is still active and has not advanced since the sweep read it (last_advanced_at unchanged), so a customer reply that is advancing the run is never cut off mid-step. A busy conversation, a failed conversation lookup, or a contact whose conversation no longer exists leaves the run active for a later sweep (the next inbound or outbound message recreates the thread, and the sweep after that can lease it); only a run with no contact is timed out without a lease.

A waiting automation never floods a contact. A contact reaching the same wait step of the same automation again supersedes the run already parked there (still pending, never one a resume has claimed), marking it failed with its log explaining why; superseding and parking happen in one account-scoped call serialized per automation and contact (park_automation_wait), so concurrent triggers still leave one parked run, so a follow-up is timed from the latest message and sent once rather than once per message. A resume claimed more than six hours after its run_at is skipped rather than executed, marked failed with the lateness in its log, so a cron outage is never followed by a burst of stale steps.

A property-share feedback request is visible in the inbox and names its property wherever free-form text is allowed. While the buyer's 24-hour window is open and their send language (their own, else the account default) is English it goes as free-form buttons naming the property (It's perfect / Not interested / Update preferences, each title within Meta's 20 characters) wired to the listing-feedback handler; otherwise the approved property_share_feedback template goes out with its rendered body stored as the message text (the template carries no property parameter, so it cannot name one). The WhatsApp message id of every request is stored on its share, and an "It's perfect" tap on that template is resolved to the share whose request it replied to by that id alone, never by time, and handled as interest in that property: recorded on listing_feedback, acknowledged by naming the property, and the agent notified. A tap that matches no stored request, or one request stored on shares of different properties (the dispatcher collapses an identical template sent twice within seconds into one message), gets the generic acknowledgement and records nothing.

Switching conversations in the web inbox never shows the previous contact's deals, notes or tags under the new contact's name: those sections render placeholders until the new contact's own rows arrive, and a response for the contact that was left is discarded if it lands after the switch.

An external listing session open on the account owner's own WhatsApp number (one a listing-collection flow started when the owner tried it on themselves, or one opened before the number was recognised as the owner's) is continued by the external listing flow, not adopted by the owner chatbot as an owner draft, so its corrections (a voice note transcribed first, as the owner flow does), confirm and attribution follow the external path the session was opened for.

A contact forwarded to the owner chatbot is announced as a saved draft only after a session row is written: a session row another call wrote for the same sender between the lookup and the insert (an insert conflict) keeps every card from both (the same person merged, anyone else appended, nothing discarded) through a compare-and-swap write scoped to the sender's account, while a card or screenshot that lands on a draft already open is written through the same compare-and-swap and follows the later-forward rule (the same person merged, a different person replaces the draft and the owner is told) unless it belongs with that draft, in which case a different person is appended and nothing is discarded: WhatsApp stamped it as sent no later than the draft's last write, allowing two seconds for its whole-second timestamps, and no more than 60 seconds before it (several cards forwarded at once, including cards delivered in one webhook payload that never wait for the lease), or it waited for the conversation lease and the draft was last written within 60 seconds (cards forwarded back to back), or it was sent as a reply to a contact-draft preview the bot sent in that conversation since the draft opened; no preview is ever built from an unsaved local copy (a draft that could not be read back is reported as saved but unshown, one already confirmed or cancelled gets no preview), the last preview the owner receives is the saved draft (each handler re-reads after sending, retrying a failed read rather than taking it as an answer and, if it never succeeds, ending on a plain notice without a Confirm button, and sends again, without a cap, until the row it showed is still the saved one), and a draft that could not be saved refunds the parse charge against that charge's own key (INB-028) and tells the owner to send it again.

Every contact draft card's Confirm button carries the version of the saved draft it shows together with a digest of the contact details it displays, including any number taken from an existing contact (an edit whose write fails sends no card, only a notice that the change was not saved), and Confirm saves only that version: a tap on a card whose draft or displayed details have since changed saves nothing and sends the current draft instead. A Confirm from a card sent before versions existed, or a typed "confirm", confirms the current draft as before.

A reply quote shows the quoted message's WhatsApp formatting rather than its markers: on web and mobile the quote renders *bold*, _italic_, ~strike~ and ```monospace``` as formatting, while plain one-line previews such as the forward confirmation and pinned banner drop the markers, so a contact's reply to a digest never shows literal asterisks around the quoted header.

Every AI charge the owner chatbot may later refund is burned under its own key, and the refund reverses only the ledger rows written under that key: at most once however often it is retried, never more than was charged, and nothing when the burn never landed. A refund call that keeps failing is queued in credit_refund_retries and retried by the hourly credit-refunds cron until it succeeds, the least-tried first; after ten failures each further failure is logged for manual reconciliation, and a refund that can be neither made nor queued is reported as failed, never as queued. Keyed burns keep the ordinary '<feature> burn' description in the credits history, and the older refund_credits_tx never takes a burn keyed '<feature>:…', so a legacy refund of the same feature cannot consume a keyed burn and leave its own charged.

A lead who says where they want to buy is matched on that place alone: a reply the qualification ladder resolves to one locality, or a message naming areas extracted from it, replaces the saved area list (pref_areas, and areas_of_interest when it holds any) with the areas that message names, so neither a locality inherited from a portal enquiry nor an older answer is kept beside them, and a locality that only the requirement history still names no longer matches a contact with stated areas. A message that adds an area (also, too, as well) or names none keeps every saved area, even when it resolves to one locality. A budget the portal lead webhook seeds from the enquired listing's price is recorded as pref_budget_anchor, and while it stands the budget caps matches but implies no half-of-max floor, so cheaper stock in the area the lead named still reaches them. The anchor is cleared by any other write of pref_budget_max, even of the same value, and when the lead states that same maximum in their own words; a stated budget keeps its implied floor.

Inbox search on web and mobile matches the text of every message in a conversation, not only the contact's name, phone, close reason and latest message: a query of two or more characters asks search_inbox_messages, which runs with the caller's own message RLS (so team and assignment scoping still apply), skips deleted messages, treats % and _ literally, searches only the archive view being shown so the other view's hits cannot crowd out its own, and returns the newest matching message per conversation; the row then previews that message, starting near the match even when the match is in a header line the normal preview hides.

Property type matching never crosses a sector: residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural seekers only ever match listings in their own sector. Within residential, a house or villa seeker also matches residential plots and a residential plot seeker (or a plot seeker who named no other sector) also matches houses and villas, both as partial type fits ranked below exact ones, unless the seeker's own words rule that type out ("no plots", "no sites or land", "no house", "no villa"); the swap applies to sale listings only, never to rentals, farm houses are not offered to plot seekers however the type is spelt, and apartment seekers still see neither.

A lead's question about the listing already in their thread is answered from that listing, never filed as a requirement: a question that refers to the shared listing ("is this still available?", "is it this pink house or the one next to it?") and states no budget, size or search intent stands the qualification ladder down and reaches the listing Q&A, so it is never met with silence. Availability is answered from the listing's status before any other matcher or model call — an Available listing is confirmed for what it is listed as, an Under Contract, Sold, Off Market, Archived or Rejected listing gets an apology with its status and a request for requirements and budget (a Sold listing is never promised an update), and a Pending Review listing is not confirmed; every other structured answer about an unavailable listing carries its status in the same message; the model grounding names the availability in words that cannot read as open, and the system prompt forbids describing an unavailable listing as available. A question that asks which house or plot is in the photo is handed to a person without a credit being spent, on WhatsApp and on the public showcase alike. The Q&A quotes prices in the crore and lakh form the inventory card and listing message use, and never repeats a locality the location line already carries. The post-approval details of an under-contract listing go out with its status note.

The listing a lead's message is about is read from the strongest signal in the thread before anything is answered from it: the message the lead quoted (by the property code in a share link or enquiry, else the listing's full title), then a listing the lead named since the latest share (a showcase enquiry seconds old), then a listing an agent has since pitched, whichever of those two was said more recently, and only then the share ledger. A quote or message naming several listings, is never guessed: it goes to a person. A question that is the lead's first word after two different listings were shared within five minutes of each other is never answered from one of them: a reader that answers one listing (photo requests, disinterest, the agent price learner) hands it to a person, and the lead Q&A answers it for every listing of the batch (INB-034). The same resolution serves the lead Q&A, photo requests, disinterest and the agent price learner.

A lead's question is answered for the listing they mean, never for whichever card happened to go last. Listings shared within five minutes of each other, with no word from the lead between them, are one batch: a question that follows, with nothing quoted and nothing said since, is answered for every listing in the batch (up to three, newest first), each under its title, so two localities are tellable apart. A message that names one of the recently shared listings (as the thread shows them, not the ledger's first-share dates) by a figure it carries (land area in any stored unit, built-up area, price in crore or lakh, bedrooms) or, without a figure, by a word only that listing's title or locality carries ("the Chikatogur one") is answered for that listing alone, and when such a message only points ("No this 40,000 sqft one") the question the lead asked in the message immediately before it is the one answered, never an older one. A demonstrative with a figure or a describing word is a reference and reaches the listing Q&A; a figure stating a requirement ("I want a 2400 sqft plot", "I want one 2400 sqft plot") still belongs to the ladder, and a rejection that points by figure ("don't like this 3 bhk one") is still recorded as a rejection. A description that fits several of the shares names nothing, a figure that fits none names nothing however well a word fits, and a quoted share wins over any description (INB-033).

The bot never answers a lead's question with a handover line ("let me check that with the team", the callback promise, the photo handover) while a human agent is handling the thread, meaning an agent has replied in that conversation within the last 24 hours: the lead hears nothing from the bot, and the assigned agent is still notified, the question is still relayed to their WhatsApp and the thread is still marked pending. A concrete answer the bot holds (from the listing's own fields, the seller's final price, a portal comparison or a grounded model answer) still goes out while an agent is live; when a question covers several listings (INB-034) only the handover parts are dropped and each remaining answer goes out under its listing's title. With no agent reply in the last 24 hours the handover line is sent, but only once: when the bot's latest message in the thread within the last 24 hours, with no agent reply after it, was already a handover line (any of the three, or the photo handover); a message Meta marked failed never counts as either the agent's reply or the bot's promise, the lead hears no second promise, a concrete answer still goes out, and the agent is notified again.

features.name: Contact records and duplicate resolution

invariants.rule: Agents can merge any two confirmed duplicate contacts from web or mobile, explicitly choose the surviving record, retain every distinct phone number and complementary profile or requirement data, and consolidate both one-to-one Inbox histories before hiding the duplicate.

From a contact's record on web or mobile, agents can share the account's property portal link from the business WhatsApp number or their personal WhatsApp; the link opens on the contact's recorded interests with Pulse attribution, the message tells a buyer to filter, shortlist and send the enquiry from the portal, an Agent-classified contact instead gets the link in agent view (mode=view) with co-broker copy about forwarding listings with their own share link, a closed 24-hour window falls back to the approved property selection template, and a personal share is noted on the contact's timeline.

From a buyer contact's record on web or mobile, agents can hand-pick up to 25 listings and send them through the showcase share flow to that contact; every send records the listings on the property share ledger, saves them to the contact's Portfolio shortlist as source 'shared' when they have an account (a buyer without one receives the same rows on first login), and the personal or business free-text message ends with a Portfolio nudge that names whether the buyer already has an account.

Removing an interested property is idempotent on web and mobile: the junction row and matching headline pointer are cleared together, an already-removed relationship is treated as success, and stale mobile cards disappear immediately.

Importing a phonebook contact on web or mobile fills the contact's first name, second name and Name Tag from the one device name with the same deterministic split: the Name Tag is the trailing role, trade, acronym or locality qualifier, the first name is the first given-name token plus any title or initial before it, and every remaining token is the second name. The split is a suggestion the agent can edit before or after saving, and it never sets salutation.

A contact's primary phone is the number every WhatsApp path addresses. When a contact has more than one number and none has been confirmed, the WhatsApp action on web and mobile asks once which number to message; the answer becomes the primary and is recorded on the contact so the question is never repeated. Any other number can also be made the primary from web or mobile; the swap keeps the old primary as an other number in the promoted number's slot, so no number is lost.

The Contacts area filter on web and mobile lists every locality stored on the account's contacts once per spelling group, read from GET /api/contacts/area-options which reads both area columns through account-scoped SQL functions, merges spellings of one locality under a shared key, and counts each contact once per group. Up to the same bounded number of groups can be selected at once on either surface; the list then shows a contact whose agent-entered or AI-extracted areas contain any spelling of any selected group, and the selection counts as one active filter.

A locality typed into the Contacts search box on web or mobile, or into the Requirements page search on web, whether alone or after "in", "at", "near" or "around", stands for every stored spelling of that locality: the search keys the typed text the same way the area filter keys stored areas and matches a contact whose agent-entered or AI-extracted areas contain any spelling in that group, on top of the plain text matches it already made. A term that keys to no stored locality changes nothing.

A WhatsApp message that names a listing (a showcase enquiry, a property code or a Click-to-WhatsApp ad of ours) sends its contact to Needs Review only when that message created the contact; a contact the account already had keeps its status while the listing is still linked and the enquiry still recorded. A personal-WhatsApp share logged from web or mobile is an outgoing share, recorded on the property share ledger and the contact's timeline, and never rewrites the contact's "Contacted about" listing.

An area saved on a contact from AI requirement extraction, a portal lead email, the contacts API, the public requirements form or the buyer portal is a locality: door, survey and plot numbers, bare numbers, and a lone block, sector, phase, stage or numbered main/cross road are dropped, entries joined by line breaks or semicolons are saved separately, and the same area is kept once whatever its case. A portal lead email files the buyer under the first address segment that is a locality, never the door number the listing address opens with.

From a buyer or owner contact's record on web or mobile, agents can send a Portfolio sign-in invite from the business WhatsApp number or their personal WhatsApp; the invite is offered only for the sides a Portfolio sign-in would link that contact to (buyer: Buyer or Owner & Buyer classification, an enquiry or a rating; owner: Owner, Seller or Owner & Buyer classification, or an owner-direct listing), an owner invite links the owner sign-in and says they can add properties themselves, the business number sends free text inside the 24-hour window and otherwise the approved portfolio_access_notice Utility template (an account notice whose URL button opens that side's sign-in path), refusing with a pointer to Settings and personal WhatsApp while it is not approved, and a personal invite is noted on the contact's timeline. An Agent contact is offered an Agent Invite first: a ConvoReal app invite whose link is minted from the account's invite seats (POST /api/beta-invites) and sent only from the agent's personal WhatsApp, never the business number, noted on the timeline, and disabled when that agent already has a ConvoReal account.

The new-contact forms (web contact form, mobile quick-add) require a name, and the mobile quick-add also captures the Name Tag; channels that create contacts from inbound data (WhatsApp, portal leads, phonebook import, the share dialog's inline creator) keep their own rules. Editing a contact on web or mobile captures the Reference (referrer, unlinked from any referrer contact once its text changes) and Notes, which edit the contact's most recent note: a first note is inserted, changed text updates it, cleared text deletes it, and mobile keeps Notes read-only until that note has loaded so a save never overwrites or duplicates a note it has not seen.

The Contacts tab counters on web (Active, Needs Review, Favourites, Transacted, Active Buyers, Archived) and mobile (the same less Archived) are read from the one account-scoped SQL aggregate contacts_tab_counts, never from per-tab count queries: it guards with is_account_member, skips merged and chain-only contacts and the team's own numbers (last eight digits of a profile phone), counts every tab but Archived over unarchived contacts, counts Transacted as active contacts with a won deal of the account, and Active Buyers as active contacts that are HOT or have enquired about a listing, so both surfaces show the same numbers for the same account.

Every chip column on the web Contacts table (Areas, Categories, Tags) shows at most two chips on one line, deduplicated and with blanks dropped, and folds the rest into a "+N" whose tooltip names the hidden values in order, so every row stays one line tall.

The web Contacts list and the mobile Contacts tab select their rows through the one shared column spec CONTACT_LIST_COLUMNS (src/lib/contacts/list-columns.ts), so a column one surface needs — the buyer-alerts consent pair the edit form reads, the avatar the mobile row shows — travels on both, and neither surface keeps a private select list that can drift.

features.name: Calendar, appointments and to-dos

invariants.rule: The calendar keeps the selected-day agenda visible and also makes every future scheduled appointment and every future dated open task discoverable.
Upcoming appointments and tasks are chronological and are not repeated in the selected-day agenda or the general to-do list.
Repeating or correcting the same scheduling instruction updates one appointment and produces one confirmation; it never creates a duplicate event.
A named person resolves only to the strongest unique contact match. Ambiguous names remain unlinked instead of being guessed.
Every explicitly named external attendee, including the property owner, is retained in the appointment audience so each eligible person receives timely reminders.
Correcting an appointment name, contact, property, or other non-time detail preserves its scheduled timestamp and reminder state.
Time corrections accept compact meridiem forms such as 430pm. A correction without a usable replacement date or time asks for clarification and never confirms an unchanged appointment as updated.

Every dated commitment a deal carries — an open milestone's target date, an unpaid payment tranche's due date and the expected close date, exactly as the deal_deadlines rule decides them (TXW-020) — is pinned on the calendar on web and mobile on its date, labelled by kind (Milestone, Payment due, Expected close) apart from every event type, listed among upcoming items, showable alone through a Deal dates filter on both surfaces, and opens the deal record. The calendar never writes or moves a deal date and never queries the milestone or tranche tables itself; the one write it offers is ticking a milestone done through the deal's own milestone route (CAL-010).

The To-dos list beside the calendar is a lightweight checklist of to-dos alone on web and mobile: appointments are never folded into it, and the quick-add takes a title, an optional due date and a priority without tagging contacts or properties, showing the date and priority only once a title is typed. Open to-dos lead the list; done ones sit in one Done group, collapsed by default, through the shared src/lib/calendar/todo-groups rule, and Clear completed deletes them after a confirmation on both surfaces. Deleting one to-do asks nothing and offers Undo for a few seconds instead (web: a toast, mobile: a bar at the foot of the screen), which puts the row back with its original id and fields; cancelling an appointment offers the same Undo, which reopens it through the Reopen path of CAL-010. A to-do added from a deal's Tasks tab keeps its deal and links back to it, and a contact or property a to-do already carries stays shown and opens the record on both surfaces; the calendar never sets those links.

Everything pinned on the calendar's visible days — appointments and deal dates — is also listed as the Schedule in date order (web beneath the Month and Week views, scrolling with the pane rather than inside its own box, and as the Agenda rows themselves; mobile on the selected day and in Upcoming), where an appointment's status is changed in place with the same actions on both surfaces (Done and Cancel while scheduled, Reopen afterwards) through PUT /api/appointments/[id], which re-arms the reminders on Reopen in the same write as the status and stamps a new reminder generation on Done, Cancel and Reopen alike (reminders_rearmed_at: every delivery claim records the generation it was made under, the cron takes over a claim from any other generation, and a reminder fetched or queued under an earlier generation is never sent), and a cancelled appointment stays on its day struck through rather than disappearing. A milestone date can be ticked done there through PATCH /api/deals/[id]/milestones/[milestoneId], which never moves the deal's stage (TXW-003); other deal dates open the record.

A done or cancelled appointment can be archived and unarchived on web and mobile through POST /api/appointments/archive, which stamps appointments.archived_at for the caller's account only and never archives a scheduled event; Archive done archives every unarchived finished event in view (web: the Month or Week in view, mobile: the whole month shown, loaded in pages), sent in requests of up to 500 so none is left out, and the route refuses a read-only member. How archived events show is one three-way setting with the same modes on web and mobile, Grey out archived by default: Grey out keeps an archived event on the calendar grid (the web month grid, Week and Team views, and mobile's month dots) dimmed and greyed, and off the Schedule, the Agenda and mobile's day and Upcoming lists; Hide archived takes it off the grid as well; List archived also lists it in the Schedule, the Agenda and mobile's lists. The setting sits in the web calendar's filter row whenever an archived event is filtered in, and in mobile's chip row whenever the month shown or Upcoming holds one. It is remembered per user in profiles.calendar_archived_view, so the same choice applies on every browser and on the mobile app: saves run in the order chosen so the last choice is the one kept, the calendar re-reads the setting when it regains focus, and an unknown stored value reads as Grey out. Hide archived is the one exception to CAL-010's cancelled event staying on its day. Reopening clears the stamp, and an event whose status is scheduled is never hidden whichever writer reopened it.

Schedule rows are sorted by date and time with the same three modes on web and mobile, Upcoming first by default: today's items lead, then the days ahead soonest first, then past days most recent first, each day in clock order with a date-only deal date leading its day. Earliest first and Latest first order strictly by date and time. The mode applies to the web Schedule list and to mobile's day and Upcoming lists.

A client reminder names the appointment the way its confirmation does: a meeting or other non-visit event by the agent's own title (calls send no client reminder), and only a site visit by its linked property. A client who already confirmed the appointment is not asked to confirm again: when they are its only recipient (counted over every contact on it, reachable or not) and their 24-hour window is open in English, the reminder goes as a free-form message thanking them for confirming, and otherwise it falls back to the approved template. The agenda never ends in a doubled full stop.

features.name: Brokerage invoicing and the deal document folder

invariants.rule: An invoice number is unique within its account and financial year and is never reused. A cancelled invoice keeps its number so the series has no gap, and an issued invoice never returns to draft.

An issued invoice prints the same content forever. Its issuer, customer and line items are snapshots, not joins, so editing the deal, contact or property it came from cannot change it; only a draft is editable.

Tax follows the place of supply: the same state charges CGST plus SGST in equal halves, a different state charges IGST at the full rate, and nil mode charges nothing and prints the exemption note. Known state codes override a stale stored mode, and the mode stored on the invoice is the one actually charged. Whether an invoice carries GST at all is a per-invoice toggle over the account default, so a registered brokerage can raise an exempt invoice and an unregistered one keeps its GST details ready; the exemption note is always snapshotted and printed only when that invoice charges no GST.

The billed amount is the deal value times the brokerage rate times this invoice's share, rounded to the rupee, and the same figure is shown on every surface. Totals are always recomputed server-side from the line items, never taken from the client.

A deal document is reachable only through an authenticated, account-scoped route that signs a short-lived URL. The deal-documents, generated-invoices and signatures buckets are private and no listing ever returns an object URL; the per-document route serves a redirect to the browser and the same signed link as JSON to the mobile app. Deleting a deal removes its stored objects, not only the rows that named them.

AI extraction proposes fields and never writes to an invoice by itself, and a full Aadhaar number is never stored: only the last four digits leave the file, enforced after the model returns rather than only asked for in the prompt.

An invoice file attached to a deal has exactly one home: a deal_documents row with category 'invoice' in the deal-documents bucket. There is no second store, and the folder accepts every file type the retired one did — including Word and Excel, because a brokerage's own invoice is often a workbook. Web and mobile accept the same types.

A deal document is staged straight into its own account-and-deal prefix under a server-signed, single-path upload URL rather than through the app, so the 50 MB the folder accepts is the size that actually uploads; the upload carries the file's real content type, without which storage refuses it, and a storage refusal is reported with its status and reason rather than as a retry prompt. Filing the row reads the stored object back: a path outside this account or deal, one nothing was written to, or a file that landed over the limit or of a type the folder does not take is refused and the object cleared, and the row records the size and type storage holds rather than the ones the caller declared.

features.name: Property listing media

invariants.rule: Walkthrough uploads accept MP4 up to 16 MB on Starter and 100 MB on every paid plan. A failed preliminary limit lookup never makes the client deny a potentially eligible file; the upload-session endpoint authorizes the plan. Large files upload directly to Supabase with resumable chunks bound to the authorized object path, while the server verifies the completed account-scoped object before attaching it to a property.

features.name: Property inventory discovery and shortlist sharing

invariants.rule: A locality selected from Google Places finds inventory stored under the equivalent undotted abbreviation, including J. P. Nagar to JP Nagar and B.T.M. Layout to BTM Layout.
Agents can select up to 25 properties from inventory and open the existing hand-picked showcase share flow with that shortlist already selected on web and mobile.
Selecting a Google Places suggestion starts a coordinate-based nearby search on web and mobile with a 10 km locality radius, while exact multi-area matching remains a separate explicit action.
Visitors can clear every selected property at once from both the public showcase shortlist bar and its review dialog.

Search-result showcase sharing recognises text, locality, radius and inventory filters on web and mobile, resolves them to the same available published listings, and preserves per-contact Showcase Pulse attribution.

tests.case: pins the resolved results for a structured search
uses the resolved ids for a location or filtered search
pins the resolved results for a structured search

invariants.rule: When a buyer-visible property status changes, every interested or previously shared contact is told the exact new status; Under Contract is never described as Sold, while internal moderation statuses are not broadcast.

Every saved property exposes its explicit enquired contacts separately from preference-ranked matches on web and mobile, excluding view-only engagement and providing direct contact, internationally prefixed calling, personal or business WhatsApp messaging, and follow-up actions subject to the user's permissions.

When an unmapped portal ad already has a guessed property, agents can accept that mapping in one tap on web and mobile, while retaining a separate path to choose a different property; multiple ad IDs from the same portal may remain mapped to one property without replacing one another.

tests.case: [PRP-008] accepts the guessed property without reopening the picker
keeps a second ad id for the same property as an alias

invariants.rule: Every property link sent from an agent contact's Share Inventory action opens in co-broker view and carries that contact's recipient identifier, so Showcase Pulse attributes opens and listing activity to the selected contact on web and mobile.

Every property or property-selection message sent through a business WhatsApp number or handed off to a personal WhatsApp chat carries a Showcase URL attributed to the selected CRM contact; business sends repair or append the tracked URL server-side, and personal sends cannot bypass recipient selection on web or mobile.
Authenticated workspace members viewing their own public showcase never create Showcase Pulse analytics events, while signed-in members of a different workspace remain external visitors.

Sharing a listing with its matching contacts on web or mobile never asks which WhatsApp template to use: both surfaces show the engine's listing template as the server will send it (same template pick, same params), let the agent choose which of the saved listing's own photos leads the message, forward that choice to the share-property send where any photo outside the saved listing is ignored, and explain before sending why a recipient outside the 24-hour window cannot be served (no listing template submitted, awaiting Meta approval, or rejected).

On the public showcase, a location that no published listing names is searched by distance only when the visitor asks for it (Enter or the Search near option): listings naming the place come first, then published Available listings within 5 km ranked by distance, shown with a distance coarsened to half a kilometre and never with coordinates.

A public showcase listing whose status is not Available (Under Contract, Sold, Off Market, Archived, Rejected, Pending Review) tells the enquirer so in the detail view and on its card, prefills the WhatsApp inquiry with a request for the latest status, and never offers the listing Q&A; a WhatsApp enquiry that names such a published listing by its property code, as a direct property enquiry, or by its exact title when the buyer was not already discussing it, is answered with an apology and its status instead of its details — never promised a site visit or owner call — and asked for their requirements and budget, with a promise to update them if it becomes available again unless it is Sold; a portal email lead matched to such a listing gets the same reply, or, when the 24-hour window is closed, the approved listing availability notice (which names the status, apologises, promises an update if it becomes available again and asks for requirements and budget) — falling back to the listing status notice when that is not approved, and always using the status notice for a Sold listing; the availability notice is never picked when Meta filed it as Marketing; every deal-driven listing status change — a board or journey move, a journey branch converted to a deal, a deal closed, reopened or deleted, a journey closed or reopened — goes through one database function that locks the listing and takes the strongest status its open and won deals hold, so concurrent deal changes cannot leave a stale status, a won deal is never overwritten, a listing another deal still holds is never released, and nothing is written or sent when the sync fails; closing or reopening a journey re-syncs every listing with a deal on it and reports a failure rather than succeeding silently; a listing that such a change returns to Available tells its enquirers it is available again, as an edit on the listing does; no status update reaches a contact who closed or rejected their enquiry on that listing, and none is sent when those closures cannot be read; outside the 24-hour window a status update goes out only on an approved Utility template, never one Meta filed as Marketing; the agent is alerted with the listing's status, and an enquiry card's Approve or Photos tap on such a listing sends that reply (once) instead of its details or photos. Pending Review listings keep the plain status note. Available listings show none of this.

Every pipeline stage stores what it means (open, committed, won, brokerage pending, brokerage paid or lost), inferred from its name only when it is created without one, and renaming a stage never changes its meaning. Moving a listing's deal into a committed stage (on the standard pipeline: deal confirmed or legal done) marks the listing Under Contract on web and mobile; a won or brokerage stage marks it Sold, a lost stage returns it to Available, and an open stage (enquiry through the owner's-meeting negotiation) sets it back to Available. The app, the mobile app and the database read the same stored type, and infer a missing one from the same words. Changing a stage's type re-syncs the deals on it and the listings they hold.

The public showcase grid lists published Under Contract listings after the Available ones, each badged with its status on the photo; they can never be shortlisted, and a saved shortlist drops one once it goes under contract. They are carried beside the Available catalogue rather than inside it, so the sitemap, business-profile structured data, project and farmland pages and every other reader of the catalogue still see Available listings only.

An unpublished (draft) listing never opens from a public link: the showcase ?property_id= link falls back to the showcase, /property/<slug> returns 404 before any redirect can reveal its canonical slug, and its link preview and preview image are withheld. The one exception is a link carrying a live share grant minted for that listing.

A listing's map pin comes from its map link first: coordinates carried by the link, or by the URL a short link redirects to, are used as they are. A link that names a place instead of a point (/maps/place/<name>, ?q=<address>) is geocoded by that name when a Google Maps key is configured, on create, on a map-link edit and in the pin-repair script, without a redirect hop when the name is already in the link. A link that resolves to neither (a dead link landing on the Maps home page) gives no pin and costs no Geocoding call, and resolving a link never throws.

An approved listing-access request is delivered outside the 24-hour window on the listing_access_approved template, which describes a full-listing link valid for 7 days, as soon as that template is APPROVED for the account. Until then it falls back to location_reveal, so approving a request never stops delivery. An exact-location approval always uses location_reveal and never the listing template. Both carry the same /reveal/<token> URL button.

The Deal Floor showcase design is one more agency design selectable on web and mobile: its fill-in-the-blank hero (kind family, locality, budget), kind tiles and board tiles all narrow the same catalogue grid as the other designs, a photoless listing shows a plot face drawn from its dimensions, area, facing and road width instead of a No Photos placeholder, and Quick Picks shortlists into the same shortlist as the cards, undoes cleanly, and offers the shortlist enquiry once three properties are shortlisted. Deal Floor draws no second filter bar: deal type, bedrooms and sort are refine pills, the Locality blank is searchable (typing narrows the listed localities, and a typed place no listing names is searched within 5 km from the same blank) and offers a listed locality together with its nearby listings (that locality first, then everything within 5 km), both from the blank and from an action beside the match count once a locality is picked, and any active search term, nearby place, extra locality or new-this-week filter shows as a removable chip beside the match count. Other designs keep the shared filter bar unchanged.

An agent's personal showcase link shows the company showcase design and 3D setting until that agent picks their own; a new member starts with no personal design, joining or leaving an account clears any personal design they carried in, saving any other profile change never stamps one on them, and the personal picker on web and mobile says it is following the company design and offers a way back to it.

An unknown or retired public listing, project, farmland, article, service, city or seller URL answers with HTTP 404, not a 200 not-found page: no loading skeleton sits above a public page that calls notFound(), and only the showcase home and the signed-in app groups stream behind one.

An enquiry carries one source name per portal ("Magic Bricks", "Housing", "99acres") whether the lead arrived by email or an agent mapped its portal ad, and unmapping an ad removes only the enquiries that mapping created, never one the lead email recorded.

tests.case: enquiry sources use one spelling per portal
maps the ad and tags every lead waiting on it

invariants.rule: Merging two contacts keeps each carried-over enquiry's source, date and notes, so a merged buyer still shows which portal or channel every enquiry came from and when.

A paid Google Maps lookup is bought at most once a month: every address geocode, pin reverse-geocode and showcase area lookup is served from the shared maps_lookup_cache before Google is called, a definitive miss is remembered for a week, and a property whose address Google could not place is stamped geocode_attempted_at and left out of the radius-search self-heal for 30 days instead of being re-geocoded on every search.

The inventory listing-party pills count the rows they list on the tab and summary tile in force: on Review and Archived they count only those listings, not the account's active total, and every non-agent listing (owner, WhatsApp and web self-listings) is Direct, so Direct plus Agent referred always equals All.

An empty inventory list says why it is empty: a filtered list names the tab and the filters that match nothing and offers Clear filters, and an unfiltered Review, Archived or All Listings tab explains that tab instead of telling the agent to create records.

The portal-ads drift banner is a warning, not an error: it says how many portal ads don't match their listings, Review expands the findings, and every finding offers fixing the portal record (web: the Post to Portals dialog; mobile: the portal listings sheet, with the expiry date and Mark removed) and opening the listing. Viewers and read-only members see the findings and open the listing, but the portal record is changed only by agents and above.

The Ads page always says whether Meta is connected: a not-connected intro with the three setup steps, a reconnect banner (ads keep running and billing on Meta; pausing or changing a budget needs a reconnect) when the connection expired or was disconnected, or a Connected chip, and a failed load shows an error with Retry rather than the empty state. Spend, reach, chats and cost per lead cover the last 30 days in the ad account's currency and show an as-of time once stale or archived, figures cached before the 30-day window (lifetime totals) are refetched once, archived ads included at most five per load, and dropped rather than labelled the last 30 days when that refetch fails, an archived ad shows no cost per lead because its spend froze at archival while leads keep a rolling window, Leads in Engine counts each contact once per ad in SQL rather than from a capped row fetch, a failed config or lead-count read fails the load rather than showing not connected or zero leads, and a budget edit submits once, cancels on Escape and shows the server's validation message inline.

The Needs attention count is the number of Available listings missing photos, a sale or rent price, or a map pin, and filtering by it on web (summary tile) or mobile (filters sheet) lists exactly those listings through the shared needs_attention API filter, with the listing-party pills splitting the same count.

The Inventory header has one primary action, Add Property, whose menu also holds every other way listings come in (import a shared link, sync from portals, import owner leads), beside Share Showcase Portal; no intake action is a separate header button.

Meta Ads has one home, the /ads page in the sidebar: Inventory has no Ads tab, an old /inventory?tab=ads link lands on /ads, and a listing card with an active or paused Meta campaign shows an Ad live or Ad paused badge that opens it.

The add and edit listing form shows a section index (Basics, Location, Area & specs, Photos & documents, Description, Owner & inquiries, Publish) that jumps to each section and ticks the ones filled in, keeps the Publish switch beside the save button in a footer that stays in view, and hides the Matching and Enquired Contacts tabs until the listing is saved.

The showcase share message is shown as the recipient will read it, with the contact's first name (or "there") and the real portal link filled in and marked, on web and mobile; the raw {name} and {portalUrl} template is only shown while editing it, and Copy Message is the primary action.

Secondary text in dark mode (text-slate-500 on the page, card and slate-800/900 surfaces, in the default and verdant themes) meets WCAG AA contrast of 4.5:1, and the slate ramp stays ordered from 400 through 500.
A project card on the Projects tab is one click to its units anywhere on the card, keeps Edit as a separate button, and reads sales as progress: "N of M units sold" with a bar at the sold share.
The inventory sort control says what it is: its trigger reads "Sort: <order>", never a bare order name.
While the Ads page loads it shows the campaigns table shape (the real header and placeholder rows marked busy), never a full-page splash, so the layout does not jump when campaigns arrive.

A listing card, on web and mobile, badges its status only when the status is not Available: an available listing shows its listing type alone, and Sold, Under Contract, Off Market, Pending Review, Rejected and Archived still show.

Portal listing records (property_portal_listings) are readable by every account member and written only by agents and above: a viewer or read-only member can neither mark a portal ad posted or removed nor change its expiry, from web, mobile or a direct client call, because the table's row-level security enforces the agent role on insert, update and delete.

The Meta Ads settings tab shows one Reconnect action when the token expired, warns when the connection expires within 14 days, lists what happens next before Connect, offers Reconnect and Disconnect while the ad account is still to be chosen, and shows Connect, Reconnect and Disconnect to the account owner only, who is the only role the API accepts.

A map link that opens a route (/maps/dir/…, ?daddr=) or a Street View panorama (@lat,lng,3a,…) is never stored or shared as pasted: on create, on a map-link edit, through WhatsApp intake and a parked pin, in the listing self-heal and in the pin-repair script it is replaced by a plain pin at the route's destination or the panorama's camera point, the destination's own coordinates or the last waypoint win over the origin and the midpoint viewport, and a pin link is kept exactly as the lister pasted it. The web form names a pasted route or Street View link for what it is.

Turning on an unmask option in the share dialog (exact location, documents, guarded photos) or changing its expiry mints no share grant: the share-wide key is minted the first time the link leaves the dialog (copy link, copy message, preview, Telegram, email, SMS), reused for every later send of that link, and a contact's own key is minted only when that contact is sent to and is never replaced by the share-wide key. Changing what a minted key reveals revokes it, closing the dialog never revokes a key already handed out, a key whose mint finishes after the dialog closed or its options changed is revoked, and a send whose key cannot be minted, or whose key went stale that way, is stopped with an error. The link, WhatsApp, Copy Message and Close stay in a bar pinned to the bottom of the client and co-broker tabs, which says whether the link is still masked, being unmasked, or unmasked. Mobile only lists and revokes keys, so it has nothing to mint.

The web share dialog names the listing in its header without a trailing full stop. Revoking an unmasked link takes two steps: Revoke, then Revoke now, with Keep to back out, matching the mobile confirmation; nothing is revoked on the first click. A listing with no documents or guarded photos offers no switch for them and instead links to the listing to add them. The paid Click-to-WhatsApp ad sits under Send from Engine, not among the share channels. With no search typed, Send personally on web, and the Share on WhatsApp and Broadcast pickers on mobile, list the eight most recently contacted reachable contacts by when they were last contacted (an edit to the contact does not count), named contacts ahead of phone-only ones; a name that is only the phone number, in its local, trunk-prefixed or international form, counts as no name and the number is shown once.

A listing can be shared as a WhatsApp catalog product card from the web share dialog and the mobile share sheet whenever the account has a Meta catalog: both show the same sync status (not synced, sync failed, indexing for 90 seconds after a sync, synced), both offer Sync now, both refuse to send until indexing has finished, and both send through the same product broadcast with the same retailer id (property code, else id) and caption, whose location never carries a guarded listing's street address. Only recipients the broadcast reports as sent are recorded on the share ledger. A sync counts as synced only once Meta's batch has finished without errors and the product is found in the catalog under that retailer id; otherwise the listing shows Sync failed with Meta's reason, so a send never reaches Meta for a product the catalog does not hold; the catalog item is priced in the account's showcase currency (INR when none is set), a sync fails rather than guessing when that currency cannot be read, and changing the account currency clears every synced item so none is offered at the old price currency; an automatic resync after an edit or approval clears the previous sync in the same write as the save, so the card is not offered while the new one is unconfirmed; the mobile sheet refuses to guess the price currency when the account's showcase settings cannot be read.

features.name: Stage-grouped buyer and property journeys

invariants.rule: Journey search finds the subject by identifying details, including normalized mobile numbers, and every active journey is classified by the most advanced stage reached by its live items, and while any of its visible items is dropped it is also listed under the account's first lost stage that still mirrors a pipeline stage; a journey with nothing live sits under that lost stage alone (falling back to the furthest stage reached when the account has none).
Closing a journey records a successful, paused or not-proceeding outcome plus a reason; archiving remains separate, and closed or archived journeys can be retrieved and reopened or restored.
Manual drag order is saved per journey mode and cannot contain duplicate subjects.

A journey item has one Notes box on web and mobile rather than a note button per stage. Saving a note records it, append-only and account-scoped, against the stage the item is at when the server saves it, resolved and inserted in one locked database statement (any stage the client sends is ignored), and every note of the item is listed newest first at whatever stage the item reaches, each tagged with its date and time and its stage name in the stage colour, plus its author. The history keeps its stage snapshot, author and creation time through closure, archival and later stage deletion.

Journey items captured automatically from WhatsApp shares stay hidden until reviewed. Both surfaces show the count and open a Captured tray where each item can be shown on the journey, all can be shown at once, or an item can be removed; showing logs an unhidden event that keeps the item's stage, and viewers can only look.

A stage card's header expands and collapses its rows, and a separate control on the header focuses the list on that stage: the other stage cards hide and the selected card is highlighted in its stage colour until the control is used again or the mode or view changes. A search runs inside the focused stage, and an empty focused stage says so and offers every stage back. On web the focused stage travels in the address so a reload keeps it. A selection whose card no longer exists shows every stage.

Inside a stage group a journey row does not repeat its stage; it shows how many of its items are still in the race with the same wording on web and mobile, greyed when there are none. Drag handles appear only when the order can actually be dragged.

Inside a stage group, an expanded journey leads with the live items resting on that stage, highlighted in the stage colour, and folds the items at other stages behind a count that opens on request; inside the lost stage group it leads with its dropped items instead, highlighted the same way on web and mobile; when nothing live rests on the stage, or outside a stage group, every item shows as before. Web and mobile share the split.

Every confirmed property share captures the contact×property pair on the journey through one server-side ledger writer, whichever surface sent it: the share sheet on web and mobile (both channels), a personal-WhatsApp or email share the agent logs, a contact's hand-picked listings, Radar sends and the bot's own listing sends; the ledger's insert trigger makes the same capture for a row written any other way, reading the visibility the writer recorded on it. A share the agent composed for one contact is visible at once; a broadcast or bot batch waits hidden in the Captured tray; re-sharing never duplicates, resurrects or un-hides a pair. The share-log endpoint counts as recorded only the shares whose ledger row and journey capture both landed and names every other requested recipient as failed, so the web share dialog, the web email share and the mobile product-card send report a share that was sent but not recorded instead of claiming it was logged.

A buyer's visit request that the WhatsApp scheduler consumes is logged as a client response on their journey branch for that listing (captured visibly at the first stage when the pair was never on the journey), and once the visit is on the calendar the branch advances to the account's site-visit stage through the same move as the board, forward only, never back from a later stage.

Journey, Board, Records and the Dashboard describe the same items: every deal with a contact and a property is linked to that pair's journey branch, created at the deal's mirrored stage when the pair was never on the journey, and on the default pipeline stage and outcome mirror both ways — a deal moved or marked open, won or lost on the Board moves its branch and sets it active or dropped; a branch moved, dropped or reactivated on the Journey moves its deal and sets it open, won or lost. Closing a journey as completed or not proceeding drops its live branches (a won branch survives completion) and marks their deals lost; reopening reactivates exactly the branches that close dropped and restores their deals; pausing and archiving change nothing. Deleting a deal drops its branch with the reason on record, and removing a branch from the Journey, on web or mobile, deletes the deal opened from it with the same document cleanup and property release as deleting it from the Board. A conversion opens the deal on the stage the branch already mirrors, a second deal for the same pair stays unlinked, and Focus counts as live only the journeys the overview still shows as active.

Journeys inside each group are ordered by most enquired by default — the buyer's or listing's enquiry count, the newest enquiry breaking ties — and can instead be ordered by the most recent enquiry, manual order, or furthest stage on both web and mobile (web also offers priority and recent activity). Journeys with no enquiry follow, most recently touched first. Drag handles appear only under manual order. Every journey row with enquiries shows the same count label on web and mobile with the latest enquiry's source and date ("3 enquiries · Housing · 12 Sep"): the source is the newest enquiry that has one, followed by "+N" when the enquiries came from N other sources, and the year is added only when it is not the current one; a journey with none shows no label. Journeys can be filtered by enquiry source on web and mobile: the filter offers every source the journeys in view have, each with how many journeys have it, most common first, keeps a journey when any of its enquiries came from the chosen source, keeps a chosen source offered while no journey in view has it, shows a clear button beside the filter while a source is chosen that returns to all sources, counts only journeys from the chosen source in the Active, Closed and Archived view tabs (the totals return when the filter is cleared), shows the chosen source first on the mobile chip row, followed by the clear chip, and scrolls that row back to its start whenever the chosen source, the buyer/property tab or the active/closed/archived view changes, so a chosen or remembered filter is always visible without scrolling, and remembers the chosen source across visits on the same browser or device, separately for each account and for buyer and property journeys, so another account signed in on that device never inherits it; a stored value that is blank or not text is ignored. Tapping the label lists the enquiries newest first — the enquired properties on a buyer journey, the enquiring buyers on a property journey — each with its source and date, opening that property or contact.

After an item on a web journey map is advanced or moved to another stage, the map centres on that item's new step and highlights it, keeping it on the map even when it now rests outside the stage group's fold. In the overview the journey stays expanded, its new stage group opens (and becomes the single focused group when one stage was focused), and the list scrolls to the journey in that group, so the fresh step is in view. Mobile does the same after a move from the journey list: the journey's new stage group opens, the journey card expands, the list scrolls to it, and the moved item stays listed and marked even when it now rests outside the group's stage. Web and mobile share the stage-group lookup.

Inside every active stage group on web and mobile, journeys are split into Focus, listed first, and Passive, folded behind a count that opens on request (and opens by itself while searching or when a moved journey lands in it); closed and archived views are not split. A journey nobody has sorted is Passive. Any agent moves a journey between the two from a one-tap control on its row or its actions menu; viewers see the split but cannot change it. The split is shared by the whole team by default; an account admin can switch it (Settings → Members on web, Edit profile on mobile) so every agent keeps their own Focus list instead, and each scope reads and writes only its own rows. The compartment is saved through /api/journey/compartments, which checks the journey belongs to the caller's account, and row-level security admits only rows of the scope in force. Neither surface splits a stage until the Focus list has loaded, and a failed load leaves the stage unsplit.

A client who types when to be checked back on — in reply to the enquiry check-in (the enquiry_checkin_notice template or an inbox check-in) or to the timeline question — gets the date read ("wait for a week", "in 10 days", "5th October"), a follow-up to-do filed at once for that contact×property (moved, never duplicated, when one is open), the journey item's planned step stamped, the unprompted-pitch quiet window set, the words logged on the journey and the agent notified; the bot then asks "shall I check back with you in a week, on <date>?" with Yes and Another date buttons. Yes acknowledges the date; Another date asks again and the typed answer moves the same reminder without asking a second time. A reply that names no date files no reminder. A reply asking to be called ("Please call me") is logged on the journey but never answered with the timeline question: it goes on to the callback handover, which promises a call and notifies the assigned agent. The client offering to ring us is not such a request, including when the offer follows "and" ("I'll check and call back tomorrow"), while "I'm busy and call me later" still is; and a reply that rejects the listing and asks to be called ("Not interested, please call me") records the rejection without the factor prompt and still reaches the callback handover.

When a forwarded client reply names no property by code or title, the property it is about is resolved from the contact first: a contact who owns exactly one listing (owner_contact_id) has it picked when the message points at no other listing and the whole inventory was read (an account too large to read in one pass is offered the owned listing rather than having it picked), and a contact who owns several, or whose message also points elsewhere, is offered their own listings first, each marked "owned by <name>". Only then is the rest of the inventory ranked by words in the message, and filler words (the, and, for, with, sale and the like) never count as a match, so a reply is never offered unrelated listings for sharing a word like "the".

When a forwarded client reply could be about a few listings, the agent is never boxed in: the message lists up to three, offers buttons for the top two plus Cancel (three in all, WhatsApp's limit), and accepts a typed property code for any listing without a button, which completes the same reply as a tap would. Cancel links nothing and creates no event, reminder or owner message; the client's words stay in their contact notes, and a later code typed in the thread no longer attaches to the cancelled reply. A tap or typed code that links a listing retires the question the same way.

Every visible, active journey branch on a stage that mirrors a pipeline stage is a deal on the Board at that stage, with no convert step: the deal opens by itself, linked to the branch, when the branch is captured visibly, shown from the Captured tray, moved or reactivated, and existing branches were backfilled the same way. A branch still in the Captured tray, a dropped branch, a branch on an unmirrored stage and a branch already linked to a deal open none; when the pair has a deal no branch holds on the mirrored pipeline, that deal is linked and brought to the branch's stage instead of opening a second one (a deal on another pipeline is never adopted); a deal that opens or is linked on a closing stage gets the standard milestone checklist, and the listing status is re-synced whenever a deal opens on a closing stage or a linked deal moves; Records lists only deals whose closing record has started (they carry milestones), so a deal opened at an early stage stays off it; a deal deleted from the Board is not reopened by the drop that follows; failing to open the deal never blocks the journey write. Neither web nor mobile offers "Convert to deal" or calls the conversion route; both open the branch's linked deal, for viewers too, and show nothing to open when there is none.
