A client who answers an inbox check-in by typing a requirement (a property type, budget or size, such as "Hsr layout 30x40 north and east facing only") that names no check-back date is not treated as an update on the checked-in listing: nothing is logged on that listing's journey, no note, deal note or notification is written for it, and the timeline question is not sent; the message falls through to requirement qualification, which files it on the contact and replies with matching listings — or, when an agent sent the check-in and so owns the thread, files it and raises a Match Radar event for the agent instead of the bot replying. When qualification will not take the message (auto-qualification off, a parked requirement, or a contact who is not a buyer), the requirement is still appended to the contact and their preferences re-extracted, so it reaches matching. References to the checked-in listing itself ("this plot", "the villa") are not a requirement, so "Not interested in this plot" stays a check-in reply while "Not interested in this plot; I need a villa under 2 crore" is matched. A requirement asked as a question ("Any villa under 2 crore?", "Can you find a villa that is under 2 crore?") counts as a requirement. A reply that rejects the listing or asks a question naming it ("Is the plot east facing?", "Is it a corner plot?", "Does this office have parking?", "Can it be used as an office?") is still handled as a check-in reply, and a reply that asks to be checked back on at a date ("check back in a week", "wait for 2 weeks", "call me after a week") still files the check-back as JRN-015 describes; a date stated as part of the requirement ("available next week", "can't wait, need a 2 BHK next week") does not, and neither does a declined check-back ("no need to check back").

Text an agent types in reply to a WhatsApp closing card ("Closing in progress") is that agent's note on the deal the card names: it is logged on that journey item and the buyer's contact notes, the card is held back for the re-nudge period, and the agent is told it was noted, without asking who the client is and without messaging the buyer. The deal is read from the quoted card's buyer phone, and its listing when the buyer is closing on more than one; when that deal is no longer on a closing stage the agent is told the note was not saved. A quote of any other message is left to the paths below.

A share the ledger could not record is never reported as recorded. The server ledger writer never throws and never turns a delivered message into a send error, but it reports whether both the ledger row and the journey capture landed. POST /api/properties/share-log answers 200 with `recorded` counting only the recipients whose writes both landed and `failed` listing every other requested contact id. Every client that logs a share through it, on web and mobile (the share sheet, a logged personal-WhatsApp or email share, the mobile product-card send), reads the answer through one shared reader that retries the failed recipients, up to three attempts, retries a transport failure the same way, stops at once on a refusal, and treats a recorded count short of the recipients sent as unrecorded. Every one of those surfaces then tells the agent the share went out but was not recorded: the web share dialog, the web Matching Contacts broadcast, the web email share, a personal-WhatsApp share logged from the web contact page or the mobile share sheet, and the mobile product card.

features.name: Saved buyer requirements and verified agent sharing

invariants.rule: A buyer requirement shared to another ConvoReal account is delivered only to the registered account resolved from a saved Agent contact, carries a structurally masked brief without buyer identity or contact details, and accepts responses only from inventory owned by the recipient account.

A tap on a button the Engine put on an agent's WhatsApp card (the closing card's advance, update request and snooze among them) runs that button's action and is never read as a forwarded client reply or relayed to a lead: every button prefix a module hands to the control dispatch is registered as an Engine control reply. When a forwarded client reply names no client, the contacts offered as candidates are nominated only by words the client wrote, or failing those the listing and brief the model read, never by the model's own summary of the thread.

A requirement can be started from the Requirements screen itself on web and mobile, without first opening the contact: the agent picks the client, then writes the brief. The picker offers only contacts whose brief the save route will write, and mobile offers Edit on no other card, so no path opens a brief the server will refuse. The picked client arrives carrying the brief already on record, so an existing requirement is shown rather than silently replaced by the one being typed. Read-only members are not offered the flow.

The account's buyer and agent requirement briefs are browsable on web and mobile from one screen: the same four counters (total, high priority, buyers, agents) each doubling as a filter, the same classification and priority filters, and one search over client, phone, brief text, notes and areas where a typed locality matches every stored spelling. Each card shows the brief the contact is actively asking about, resolving an active requirement profile when there is no primary statement, with explicit preferences winning over AI-extracted ones and the extracted ones marked as such.

A brief shared to a co-broker from either surface carries the same text: masked mode states an opaque REQ- reference and withholds the client's name, the agent's tags and notes, full mode carries them, and a parked or empty brief is never sendable. Mobile builds the message from its own copy of the digest rules, which must produce output identical to the web module for every brief and mode.

The Shared requirements search on web and mobile matches a share whose brief names a locality the typed text asks for under any spelling, alone or after "in", "at", "near" or "around", using the same spelling key as the Contacts area filter, on top of the plain text match over reference, sender, requirement text, areas, projects and property types. A term that keys to no locality changes nothing.
Primary and additional saved buyer requirements remain independently editable and deletable on web and mobile; deleting one brief never deletes the buyer contact or unrelated saved briefs.

features.name: Deals board — every stage in one row, with the wheel kept as a choice

invariants.rule: The Deals board opens flat on both surfaces: every stage of the pipeline in one row, active stages first in position order and then the won and lost stages at the right edge whatever their stored position, an empty stage folded to a rail that still accepts a drop and opens on a tap. The rotating wheel is a per-device choice behind a Flat / Wheel switch, stored under one key on both surfaces, and never the default.

One fee rule on every board surface: a deal's fee is its saved brokerage amount, else its recorded rate applied to the value, net of co-broker payouts, and a deal with neither has no fee and says "Fee not set" — never a guessed 2%. A stage header leads with the deals' value and shows fees only once some are recorded; the Deals shown tile counts every deal the Focus / All switch is showing, lost ones included, the same number the switch carries. Web and mobile compute these through the same module.

Every amount on the Deals surfaces — board cards, stage headers, stat tiles, closing-record rows and the deal workspace — prints in one Indian compact notation (₹8.16 Cr, ₹75.05 L, ₹95,000); other currencies render through Intl.

A deal card names the property and the buyer once: the headline is the property (unit number first when it has one), the contact row names the person, and the deal's own title appears only when it says something the headline does not.

features.name: Transaction Workspace — the closing record for a deal

invariants.rule: Converting a journey item opens exactly one deal, preserves provenance through source_journey_item_id, lands on the first active (never terminal) pipeline stage whatever the board order, seeds the default board service-side when the account has none, and leaves the journey and its history untouched; converting again returns the same deal.

deal_events is insert-only: authenticated roles hold SELECT and INSERT alone, the INSERT policy pins actor_id to the caller, and a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE from every role except the cascade from a deleted deal. No client edits a timeline entry.

Milestones and pipeline stages are independent: completing, skipping or reopening a milestone never changes the deal's stage or the property's status, and a stage change never completes a milestone. Both surfaces label milestone statuses identically.

Agreed consideration, registered consideration, other component, token, TDS, instrument references and brokerage received are internal-only: they are deny-listed from every external representation of a deal, never selected by /api/v1 or a public route, and never carried on a timeline event as a value.

An external audience over a bundle sees only the deals it is party to — a seller on one plot never sees the other plot's seller, terms, notes or side-only items — and a stranger sees nothing, not even an id. Every external projection passes through src/lib/deals/visibility.ts.

Token money has one source of truth per deal: a deal linked to an Owners Den room derives it from token_escrows and refuses token writes at the API and by database trigger; any other deal records token/advance directly. Both surfaces hide the token fields when Token Safe owns them.

A deal document's status only moves forward (draft → reviewed → approved → executed); approved and executed documents are superseded by a newer upload and kept, never deleted; a superseded document cannot change; all three rules hold at the API and by database trigger; expiry is a date the workspace surfaces. Both surfaces label statuses identically.

Every Transaction Workspace mutation (conversion, events, milestones, financials, documents, bundles, deal tasks) refuses read-only members through requireWriteRole, while reads remain available to viewers.

A stakeholder is a name, a role and a side on one deal and never a login. A share link is minted per stakeholder for the buyer or seller side only, its token is stored as a SHA-256 hash and shown exactly once, it expires within 30 days, it can be revoked, and every open and document fetch is logged with a hashed address. Both surfaces name the same roles, sides and expiry choices.

Every external representation of a deal — the portal view, a bundle sibling, a document fetch — is built by src/lib/deals/external-view.ts through the visibility resolver; a public deal-share route never selects a financial column, never builds its own payload, and re-checks document visibility at the byte boundary. Progress counts the whole checklist so a partial view is never presented as complete.

A sensitive link demands a per-token one-time code: six digits, hashed with the server key and bound to the link, at most five attempts, expiring in ten minutes; a successful check yields a signed unlock for that one link that expires in thirty minutes. No Supabase Auth user, session or cookie is ever created for a stakeholder, and the link itself is handed over by the agent through the share sheet or wa.me, never sent by the app.

Every timeline entry, milestone and document carries a visibility that defaults to internal; an event's visibility is fixed at insert because deal_events is immutable; notes, milestones and documents offer the same four visibilities on both surfaces.

A published update is a durable snapshot: deal_updates is insert-only (SELECT/INSERT grants, published_by pinned to the caller, UPDATE and DELETE refused by trigger except the cascade from a deleted deal), its audience is never internal, it quotes only milestones and timeline entries every reader may already see, and a correction is a new update naming supersedes_update_id while the original stays. Both surfaces compose over the same routes with the same quoting rule.

Delivery is decided honestly and recorded separately: the business number sends free-form only inside the recipient's 24-hour window and the approved purchase_progress_notice template only to a buyer outside it, personal WhatsApp is a wa.me handoff the app never sends, and sent, opened and acknowledged are three timestamps on the recipient row that are never inferred from one another. Both surfaces name the same channels and stages.

Published updates reach a stakeholder only through the external view and the visibility resolver: a side sees its own and shared updates newest first, a corrected update stays visible and marked, and an acknowledgement is recorded against the recipient row addressed through the link that resolved, never against the update as a whole.

The Records view names every row by buyer and property (unit number first), demotes a requirement-style deal title to a second line without ever repeating a converted title, and lists only closing records, which are the deals carrying milestones, never a journey link alone: a deal starts its closing record (the standard milestones) the moment it enters Negotiation/Token or a later non-lost stage through PATCH or PUT /api/deals/[id], which the board, the workspace header and mobile all use to move a stage, pausing for brokerage before a capture stage exactly as the board does, on web and mobile alike.

Deals is one surface with three views of the same rows (Board, Journey, Records) on web and mobile; the old /pipelines, /journey and /automations?tab=pipelines addresses keep landing on the matching view with their query carried across, and Automations holds automations, flows and analytics.

Journey stages are mirrors of the account's default pipeline stages (one journey stage per pipeline stage, same name, colour and order, kind derived from the stage's stored type in SQL and TypeScript); there is one stage editor, the pipeline's, and a pipeline stage cannot be deleted while journey items sit on or plan for its mirror; a converted deal and its journey item stay on the same stage whichever side moved, with the journey keeping the move in its history; every journey move — web, mobile and the WhatsApp closing card — runs through one move function, and onto a mirrored stage it runs the same stage-move logic as the board (brokerage capture, closing record, property status) while a deal on another pipeline keeps its own stage; and moving a journey item into a closing or won stage opens its closing record on that very stage.

A bundle is created only through POST /api/deal-groups, from two to twenty deals none of which is already bundled; every member stays its own deal with its own seller, milestones, documents and terms, and the bundle only reports combined progress. Web and mobile both offer the picker from the record header, list the same buyer's deals first, pre-tick them, propose the same default name and enforce the same limits, and open the bundle's members from the same chip.

A milestone target date or expected close date on a live deal is a deadline: one SQL rule (deal_deadlines, guarded by is_account_member, and its service-role twin deal_deadlines_for_account) decides which are due, and Focus on web and mobile, the web Today page, the calendar on web and mobile (CAL-008) and the agent task digest all read it rather than querying milestones themselves. A completed or skipped milestone, a deal with an actual close date, and a won or lost deal never surface. Overdue, due today and due soon are labelled identically on both surfaces, and the digest reminds only the deal's assigned agent (or the opener of an unassigned deal), over a shorter window than the screens look ahead.

A deal's payment schedule is one row per tranche in deal_payment_tranches, written only through /api/deals/[id]/tranches: a label and an amount are required, a receipt is a date and optionally a part amount, and a tranche with money against it is corrected, never removed. The table is internal only like the other financials (never /api/v1, a public route or a stakeholder link) and amounts never ride a timeline event. Scheduled, received and outstanding are summed on the server and shown, not recomputed, on web and mobile; both label a tranche received, part received, overdue, due today or scheduled by the same rule; and an unpaid tranche's due date is a deal deadline through the same SQL rule as milestones.

The Records index carries each deal's expected and actual close dates from transaction_workspace_index and both surfaces show them by one label rule (closes, close date passed, closed) and sort by one rule (soonest expected close first, undated after dated, closed deals last) when the agent chooses Close date over Recent.

Co-broking: a deal's brokerage fields stay what the brokerage collects, and each other broker it pays out of that commission is one row in deal_co_broker_payouts, written only through /api/deals/[id]/co-broking (with the deal's position: direct, buyer's side, seller's side or in the middle). A payout needs a broker and an amount, may name a broker stakeholder on the same deal, and once paid is corrected, never removed. deals.co_broker_payout_total is the trigger-kept sum, and every revenue figure (dashboard metrics, pipeline donut, team and lead-source analytics, the board, pipeline analytics and the deal card on web and mobile) counts the brokerage's own share: collected less payouts, floored at zero. Position, payouts and the total are internal only like the other financials (never /api/v1, a public route or a stakeholder link) and amounts never ride a timeline event. Collected, paid out, still to pay and your share are summed on the server and shown, not recomputed, on web and mobile.

Every dashboard revenue function (dashboard_metrics, dashboard_pipeline_donut, team_analytics, lead_source_analytics) counts the brokerage's own share of a deal: its brokerage, or the 2% fallback, less deals.co_broker_payout_total (the trigger-kept sum of what it pays co-brokers, which no client can write and whose upkeep never moves the deal's updated_at), floored at zero only when there are payouts, keeping each function's is_account_member guard and SECURITY DEFINER. A deal with no payouts reads exactly as before.

Marking a deal lost asks why, on web (board drag, deal form, workspace header) and mobile (move sheet, deal screen, edit form): one of Price disagreement, Terms disagreement, Owner backed out, Buyer backed out, Legal or document issue, Financing fell through, Bought elsewhere or Other, with a note that Other requires. The deal routes refuse a lost status without a reason (unless the deal was already lost) and any unlisted reason, the reason and note show on the lost deal's card, a deal marked lost carries its reason to its journey branch's drop reason and a journey branch dropped with a reason carries it to its deal, and reopening a deal clears both. The web deal form asks once: Mark as Lost uses the reason already picked in the form's inline panel, and with none picked it moves the form to the lost stage and points at that panel instead of opening a second prompt. Moving a deal that is already lost, with a reason on record, to another lost stage (board drag and workspace header on web, move sheet and deal screen on mobile) keeps that reason instead of asking again.

The Board on web and mobile opens on Focus: it shows only deals whose buyer or listing journey is in the Focus compartment (by the account's team or per-agent Focus setting) and still active on the Journey (not paused, closed or archived), decided once in board_focus_deal_ids for both surfaces, with a Focus / All switch that shows every deal on the pipeline; the stage counts, column totals and stage wheel follow the switch, moving a journey between Focus and Passive refreshes the Board, and while Focus is loading or has failed the Board shows a loading or error state with a way to All rather than every deal. On web each stage column scrolls its own cards inside a bounded height, so a busy stage never stretches the page.

On web the active and successful stages sit on a ring that turns full circle: the focused stage faces the centre with the stages before and after it fanned out on both sides (the last stage sits left of the first), every stage's heading chip rides directly above its own column and turns with it, and the ring turns the same way from a grab anywhere on it, a horizontal trackpad or shift-scroll, a chip, the arrows and the arrow keys, settling on the nearest stage (further after a flick). Dragging a deal flattens the ring so a drop lands where it is seen even while it turns, and holding the deal at either edge keeps turning it a stage at a time.

An open New Deal or Edit Deal form on the web Board keeps what was typed when the browser tab regains focus or the session token refreshes: those auth events never send the Board back to its full-page loading state or reload its pipeline list; that state shows only while the pipelines first load, when the signed-in user or account actually changes (so another account's board is never left on screen), or while a pipeline's Focus list loads for the first time.

A deal created on web or mobile (POST /api/deals) lands on the Board's default Focus view at once: the server puts its buyer's journey (or its listing's, when it has no buyer) in Focus, in the team split or the creating agent's own by the account's Focus scope, only for a buyer or listing in the caller's account, and a failed Focus move never fails the creation. The Focus move never reopens a journey, so a deal whose journey is paused, closed or archived stays under All as TXW-026 requires. After any deal save, stage move or delete, from the deal form, the Board or the deal record, both surfaces refresh the Focus board, the transaction records and the dashboard.

A closing record opens on where it stands, not on a form: Overview shows the next pending milestone with a tick that completes it through the milestones route, the open tasks, the latest timeline entry, the people on each side and a money summary (deal value, brokerage, collected, outstanding, token, payment schedule), and the financial forms, payment schedule and co-broking live on a Money tab that sits right after Overview on both surfaces.

Milestones are a checklist: the tick is the primary control on every row, the meta line reads Due / Done / status / visibility, and a row's status, visibility and due-date controls appear only when its options are opened.

A timeline entry is attributed to the member who made it, to the stakeholder who acknowledged an update over WhatsApp, or otherwise to "System" when no member is behind it, whatever free text or source the writer stored; the source is shown only for mobile and API entries. Web and mobile apply the same rule.

features.name: Saved WhatsApp numbers — switch the live number without a PIN

invariants.rule: Every successful Official API save (settings form, guided setup, sandbox upgrade) records the number as a saved profile keyed by phone_number_id with its encrypted token and registration state; a re-save refreshes the same profile; a phone number saved by another account, live or not, cannot be claimed.

whatsapp_config stays the single live number. Activating a saved profile keeps the outgoing number saved, copies the profile's credentials and registered_at into whatsapp_config after Meta accepts the saved token, never calls /register, and refuses to touch the live row when Meta rejects the token; the live profile cannot be deleted; summaries never carry a token.

Registration state is read from Meta (platform_type CLOUD_API), never assumed: a save without a PIN, the Verify with Meta probe, and a profile switch all record registered_at as null with Meta's reason when Meta reports the number unregistered, and a declined display name is named as that reason. A number Meta exposes no platform for (test numbers) keeps its saved state.

A switch of the live Official API number (profile activation or a save that replaces the number) records the previous display number and the switch time on whatsapp_config, and the number-change window is open for exactly seven days from that time. contact_number_update is a Utility engine template in every product language with one acknowledgement button, addressing the contact, the brokerage and the previous number.

Only a contact with one-to-one WhatsApp message history from before the switch is told about the number change, at most once per new number, whether by the notify-recent-contacts action or as the precursor the dispatcher sends ahead of any routine message inside the window: the ledger row is claimed before sending, released when the send is skipped or fails, and the notice goes free-form inside the contact's 24-hour window and by the approved template outside it, never by an unapproved template. New contacts never receive the notice, and the notice itself is never preceded by another notice.

A saved number that is not live may auto-reply to inbound messages, never the live number: the switch is refused on the live profile and cleared on activation; the reply goes from the retired number itself, quotes the inbound message, names the live number with a tap-to-chat link (or renders the saved custom message's placeholders), is sent at most once per sender per 24 hours with the ledger claimed before the send and rolled back when Meta rejects it, and every inbound message to the retired number is surfaced to the account owner as a notification whether or not a reply went out.

A phone number id or WABA id is digits only. The settings save, the sandbox upgrade and the admin sandbox routes answer 400 for anything else before Meta or the database is touched, and the Graph helpers that address a number or a WABA by id (verify, register, subscribe, subscribed apps, registration state, permission check, and the free-form text send) refuse a malformed id without sending a request.

features.name: Contact language — the language every outbound message goes out in

invariants.rule: Every outbound template send resolves its language as contacts.preferred_language first, accounts.default_language second, English last. A null contact language means unknown and inherits the account default; an explicit 'en' is a choice and overrides a non-English account default. Language is one value per contact, never per action or per channel.

The contact's language is visible on the contact record and changeable in one tap on web and mobile, without opening the edit form, through PATCH /api/contacts/[id]/language. The picker offers exactly the product languages plus a follow-the-account-default choice, the route accepts only those codes or null, and it writes one column scoped to the caller's account.

Every language of a template shares the category Meta fixed for its name: once any variant has reached Meta, a draft or submission of another language goes out under that Meta-held category (an approved variant's category first, any Meta-held variant's otherwise), never the builder's request, and the response names the requested and assigned categories whenever they differ. A name no language of which has reached Meta keeps the requested category.

A non-English engine template has exactly one door to Meta while it is behind the review gate: the review strip's Submit to Meta, shown only after sign-off; the generic per-row Submit and Resubmit are not offered on such a row. The strip disappears while Meta holds the row pending, approved or paused, so a live translation is never offered for resubmission. A translation Meta rejected returns behind the gate: it is reworded locally, signed off again, and re-submitted through the Meta edit, which the edit route refuses (409) for an unreviewed row or for wording that differs from the signed-off body and footer. English and account-authored templates keep the generic Submit, Edit and Resubmit.

A submit Meta refuses because the language already exists is not a failure: the route looks up the variant Meta holds for that name and language and adopts its id, status, category and content (header, body, footer, buttons, samples, as Meta returns them), so the local row ends as a sync would leave it and never claims Meta holds words it refused. A refused submit of any other kind records only submission_error on a row that already carries a Meta template id, never rewrites that row's status or clears its id, and writes nothing at all when the lookup itself fails. Every submit button (one-tap engine, reviewed translation and the dialog) ignores a second click while a submit is in flight.

A send picks the recipient's language, except while Marketing to that recipient is paused, when a deliverable Utility variant of the same template wins over a Marketing one in their language. Two layers enforce it: the template loader prefers an approved Utility variant (their language, then English, then any) once it reads the contact's pause, and the dispatcher — which every send path goes through — swaps a paused Marketing send onto an approved Utility variant of the same name when it fits the parameters already built, matching the body placeholder count and the header kind, refusing the send only when none fits. A Utility variant in the recipient's own language is always the best answer, an unapproved row never beats an approved one, and a name with no fitting Utility variant behaves exactly as before.

features.name: Guidance value — Karnataka government value of a property from its sale deed schedule

invariants.rule: A schedule read is one Gemini call over an uploaded PDF or photo of at most 4 MB. Staff pay guidance_value_lookup credits, burned before the read and refunded when it fails; Portfolio buyers and owners read free under a per-person daily limit. An unsupported or oversized file is refused before any charge, and re-matching an edited schedule never reads or charges.

Matching ranks imported rates by area, road and survey number against the schedule and prefers the rate column for the schedule's type and usage: a road-specific rate of the right block beats an area-wide one, a different block or stage is demoted, and a rate whose area name shares nothing with the schedule is never offered. A schedule that names a district is matched only against that district's rates, and a subdivided survey number such as 45/2 is never treated as covered by 45/1.

Value is rate converted to per sq.ft times area: land or site area for site, house, agricultural and industrial rates, built-up area for apartment rates, plus an optional building component. A missing area yields no value and names the area to enter; a built-up area is never used as land extent.

A saved guidance value belongs to one account and a property or transaction of it, and is written only by POST /api/guidance-value/saved: members have no direct insert policy. The total is recomputed on the server from the stored rate and a snapshot of that rate is kept, so a client-sent total is ignored and deleting a notification does not change saved values.

A platform admin can import notifications straight from the IGR website: the server lists the PDFs in the guidance value table (district carried down each spanned row, Bengaluru registration districts mapped to Bengaluru Urban, BDA corrigenda listed separately) and downloads the chosen ones. Only https links on karnataka.gov.in are fetched, every redirect is re-checked against that allowlist, pages and PDFs are size-capped, and a download that is not a PDF is refused.

A platform admin can upload many notification PDFs at once: the SRO and district are guessed from each file name (Bengaluru registration districts and old district names included), fall back to a default district, stay editable per file, and each file is uploaded and read in turn. Files that are not PDFs by their %PDF- signature, or are over 14 MB, are skipped before any upload. Stop halts before the next parse starts, and retrying a stopped or failed file resumes its existing source instead of uploading it again.

The Guidance Value Import Chrome extension imports every IGR notification with one click and no manual steps: it reads the rendered IGR page in the admin's browser and hands the HTML to ConvoReal, which maps rows to districts and SROs and reports each PDF's existing source and status without fetching IGR itself; imported notifications are skipped, unfinished ones resume, and new PDFs are registered with their karnataka.gov.in source_url (any other source_url is refused) before the extension drives the parse to completion. A source whose PDF never finished uploading is reported by the parse endpoint as 409 SOURCE_NOT_STORED, and the extension deletes and re-uploads it instead of looping; PDF downloads are capped at 14 MB while streaming.

A Gemini outage never burns through an import run. When Gemini refuses a guidance value parse for billing, depleted credits or an invalid key, the parse endpoint answers 503 AI_UNAVAILABLE and leaves the source's status and progress untouched so it resumes; a Gemini rate limit answers 429 AI_RATE_LIMITED. The Chrome extension pauses the whole run on AI_UNAVAILABLE and waits a minute and retries on AI_RATE_LIMITED, pausing after ten waits. Rate parsing uses GEMINI_IMPORT_API_KEY when it is set, so imports cannot exhaust the key other AI features share.

Rate parsing never resends the whole notification: each Gemini call receives an excerpt of only the pages being transcribed plus the page before them for heading context, with instructions mapping excerpt pages back to notification page numbers and, for an interactive read, the headings of the last saved row (by page, then insertion seq) carried forward (a batch carries them across ranges after reading, GVL-012); rows Gemini returns from the context page are dropped. A PDF that cannot be loaded, copied or saved by pdf-lib falls back to sending the whole file.

Rate parsing draws from the import-scoped keys of the AI key pool (AIK-001) and falls back to the general keys, or to GEMINI_IMPORT_API_KEY, when none is managed; it runs on the lite model tier unless GEMINI_IMPORT_TIER is 'standard'.

The schedule reader also reads a Karnataka RTC (Pahani): it records document_type 'rtc', drops the village code, transliterates Kannada names letter by letter without substituting a similar-sounding place, keeps the village as printed in village_local and the extent as printed in extent_printed, joins survey and hissa as the survey number, and fills land_area only when the extent's column units are certain, otherwise leaving it for the user to enter. Web and mobile show the as-printed village and extent under the summary with the same wording. Rate ranking compares place names by a spelling key that ignores doubled letters, aspirated consonants, long-vowel spellings and a trailing vowel, so Adduru matches a notification's Addur but not Adyar; when the district is known, candidates are also fetched by that key (search_guidance_value_rates_by_place_key over the indexed guidance_place_key of village and locality, which mirrors placeKey and ignores bracketed text and the words village and grama, so a notification's "Addoor Village (Gurupura Hobli)" still matches Adduru), so a spelling too far apart for trigram search is still found, and the key lookup never runs without a district.

Agricultural guidance values keep the land class of the column they were printed in: the reader asks Gemini for separate codes for dry land (Khushki / Punja), wet land (Tari / Nanja), garden land (Bagayat) and plantation (coconut, arecanut, coffee), stores it as guidance_value_rates.land_class, and falls back to no class only when the column names none. Web and mobile show the class after the property class in the rate line with the same wording.

When a notification's text layer states its rate unit in a header ("per Sq.Mtr", "Rate per sq.ft", "ಪ್ರತಿ ಚದರ ಮೀಟರ್"), and states only one of square metres or square feet that way, every read of that notification (interactive or batched) tells Gemini that unit, to be used for site and building rates unless a table on the pages prints its own; land units keep their column. Units mentioned outside a rate header (a project's measured area, a site-size category, the carpet-area conversion note) are ignored, and stored rates are never relabelled after the fact, because a rate stored in the wrong unit is not always a unit mix-up (per-acre figures have been stored as sq ft).

Rates a notification prints in lakhs or crores ("Rs. in lakhs per acre", "ಲಕ್ಷಗಳಲ್ಲಿ") are stored in full rupees: the reader asks Gemini to mark such a column's unit as lakh/<unit> or crore/<unit> and copy the printed number, and the sanitiser multiplies by 1,00,000 or 1,00,00,000 and stores the plain unit. The sanitiser never scales by a rate's size; only the reader decides, and besides a printed lakh or crore header it treats a per-acre land column with no other printed land unit (the lakh is often stated only in the Kannada header) with figures under 1000 as lakhs, because no Karnataka land is valued under 1,000 rupees an acre; it never does so for a column printed per gunta, hectare, sq m or sq ft. On a village line that prints land rates followed by a gramathana site rate, the land columns keep their land codes and only the site column is a site rate.

A notification page that prints no column header of its own continues the table on the page before: each interactive read passes Gemini the rate columns of the last page already read (codes and units, left to right, taken from the stored rows) and asks it to use exactly those for a page without its own header, and the single-page fallback carries them from page to page. A site or building figure of 1000 or more that Gemini writes in a lakh or crore row is the site column misplaced: it is stored unscaled at that site column's unit (from the carried columns, else the notification's header unit) and dropped when neither is known; land figures are never dropped this way. The carried columns apply only to the first page of a read; a later page without a header continues the page before it in the same read. Batch reads get no carried columns, because their chunks are prepared before any page is read, but each batch chunk records the notification's header unit so a misplaced site figure is kept at that unit there too.

Before any page of a notification is sent to Gemini, its text layer is read locally (pdf-lib, decoding each font's ToUnicode map) and pages that are positively identified as not rate tables are skipped without a request: the preamble before the first rate page (gazette header, instructions, amenities lists, pages with almost no large numbers, at most the first thirty pages), pages naming a ready reckoner, construction cost, floor-rise or car-parking table that carry no rate words, and the pure numeric grids that continue such a page. A page is never skipped when its text is blank or garbled, when it carries rate words (village, hobli, road, survey, ward, block, PID numbers), or when no page in the notification reads as a rate table. Skipped pages count as read: the batch planner records them as request-free chunks and the interactive reader advances over them, so progress stays contiguous.

Every guidance value read, interactive or batched, caps Gemini's output at RATE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, and a response that hits the cap counts as unread rather than as data. Interactively the range is then read one page at a time; in a batch the range's pages are remembered on the notification (single_pages) and the next queue run submits them singly, and a single page that still overflows marks the notification failed and drops its queue request instead of being resubmitted every run. The tokens Gemini reports as thinking are logged separately (thought_tokens) on every call.

Reading a notification range interactively has one deadline (RATE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS) for the whole Gemini call, shared across the fallback model chain so a stalled request is never retried on every model. When a two-page range misses the deadline, its pages are read one at a time, each with its own deadline and with the previous page's last headings as context, so one range the model stalls on no longer blocks the rest of the notification; three deadlines stay under the parse route's 300-second limit.

Every stored rate and notification carries one canonical Karnataka district name. A rate keeps the district printed above it only when that heading is exactly a district or one of its old spellings (Bellary, Bagalkot, Bangalore, Bengaluru Urban District); a taluk, town, placeholder, page number or multi-district heading is replaced by the notification's district. A notification's district label (a registration office such as Basavangudi, or an old spelling) is filed under its district when uploaded or imported.

A queue request is remembered on every waiting notification (batch_requested_at) before any batch is built, so the guidance-batches cron keeps queuing requested notifications that one time-limited request did not reach, with its own shorter budget, even after the admin leaves the page. The cron never queues a notification nobody asked to batch; the request is cleared when the notification is ready, when its PDF cannot be read, or when a batch returns without advancing its progress, and when its batch fails, is cancelled or expires, so an unreadable range or a failed batch is not resubmitted every 15 minutes. The cron's queue budget is what remains of one route deadline after polling, and it skips queuing when too little time is left.

Rate parsing asks Gemini for compact output: rates are grouped under their district, taluk, hobli and village headings written once per group, and each table line is one array carrying locality, road, survey numbers, unit, page and a map of short class codes to rates. Headings are copied only as printed, never inferred from a recognised place name, and construction-cost, floor-rise, parking, ready-reckoner, example and general-guideline tables are skipped. The parser expands each code into its own stored rate, carries group headings into the next group that omits them, drops rows (and heading carry) from a non-rate table the model returns anyway, drops context-page rows, and still reads the older one-object-per-rate format.

A platform admin can queue every unfinished notification as a Gemini Batch API job at half the interactive price, from Admin or the import extension. Each notification's PDF is loaded once and each unread two-page range becomes one request with the page before it for context; batches stay under the inline size limit, each notification is claimed (batch_id set only where it is still empty) before anything is sent to Gemini so overlapping runs never submit it twice, a notification whose PDF is missing from storage with no pages read is marked failed and the extension deletes it only through DELETE ?unread=1 (no pages read, no batch) before re-uploading, while a PDF that only fails to download is left untouched for the next run, and a queued notification is never read interactively (the parse endpoint answers 409 SOURCE_IN_BATCH). A cron every 15 minutes collects finished batches with the key that submitted them, saves each range's rates with all headings carried across range boundaries only into leading rows that name no heading of their own, and a missing taluk or hobli carried from the previous row when district and taluk match (ignoring case and a 'Taluk' suffix), advances progress only over ranges read without a gap, logs every response's tokens under guidance_value_source_batch (priced at half in Admin → AI keys), and frees the notifications of a failed, cancelled or expired batch so they can be queued again.

features.name: AI keys — managed Gemini key pool with usage and estimated spend

invariants.rule: Every Gemini text and embedding call draws its key from the managed pool: enabled ai_provider_keys rows ordered by priority, decrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY and cached in-process for a minute, so both Vercel and the Railway worker pick up a new key without a redeploy. Import-scoped keys serve only the guidance value import, which shares the general keys when it has none; a pool holding only import keys leaves ordinary calls on the environment keys. When no general key is managed or the table is unreachable, the pool is GEMINI_API_KEY plus the comma-separated GEMINI_FALLBACK_API_KEYS, each entry either a bare key or label=key. Every feature decides whether AI is available from this pool (hasGeminiKey), never from GEMINI_API_KEY alone, so a deployment whose keys are all managed needs no Gemini environment variable.

A key refused for depleted credits, billing or an invalid key rests for ten minutes and a rate-limited key for one; the call moves to the next ready key, an ordinary model error never switches keys, a resting key is never called before its time, and when every key rests the call fails at once with the soonest key's failure. A managed key's rest and last error are written to its row and re-read on every call (only the ciphertext is cached), so every instance and the admin panel see the same state and a rest recorded elsewhere keeps its original failure message. A successful call clears the key's last error — at once when the instance knew of an error, otherwise with its next last-used write (at most a minute later) — so the admin panel never shows a recovered key as still failing, even when another instance recorded the failure.

Key material is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted and never leaves the server: the admin API returns a four-character hint only, refuses malformed labels and keys (any printable key of 20–300 characters without spaces is well-formed, since Google issues more than one format), tests a new key with one tiny call and refuses it only when Google rejects it (a valid key that is out of credits or rate-limited is saved with a warning), sends keys URL-encoded, and is open to super_admin profiles alone. Admin tooling — no mobile counterpart.

Usage comes from ai_call_log, which records the serving key's label for generation, embedding and Gemini image calls alike and is switched on by migration (the panel warns and offers to turn it on when it is off); the panel shows per key calls, tokens and estimated spend for today (Asia/Kolkata), this month and since the last recorded top-up, an estimated remaining balance of top-ups minus that spend (Google exposes no balance) computed over a window that reaches back to the month start and the last top-up, marked partial beyond the 90-day log, and labels seen in the log that are not managed. Spend is tokens × per-model USD prices with family fallbacks, overridable in system_settings; thinking tokens count as output tokens, as Gemini bills them.

When a key is refused for depleted credits, billing or an invalid key, and when every key in the pool is resting, every super_admin profile gets an in-app, push and WhatsApp notification (type ai_key_alert) naming the key and pointing at Admin → AI keys. A rate limit never alerts. Each key alerts at most once per six hours, recorded on the key row (last_alert_at) or, for environment keys and the all-resting case, in system_settings.ai_key_alerts, so several instances do not repeat it; alerting never blocks or fails the AI call.

Credits are bought in Google, never in ConvoReal: Google exposes no API to pay for Gemini credits. Each managed key card offers Buy credits, which opens Google Cloud billing in a new tab signed in as the key's label when that label is an email (authuser), and plain billing otherwise; the admin then records the top-up on the card for the estimated balance. Admin tooling — no mobile counterpart.

A model Google has retired for a key ("no longer available to new users", not found, or not supported for generateContent) never ends a call: the call moves to the next model in its tier's chain, and that key skips the model for the rest of the process while other keys keep it. By default the lite chain runs gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash and the standard chain gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash, and neither chain carries gemini-2.5-flash, which Google stopped serving to the managed key on 2026-09-26; each model carries its own quota, so a key over quota or retired on one model still answers on the next. When every model in a chain is retired for a key, the call moves on to the next ready key without resting this one, and later calls try the full chain again rather than none.

A daily cron (/api/cron/gemini-model-lifecycle) probes every model in the default chains, plus every successor already adopted, with one tiny call on each ready key. A model is recorded retired in system_settings.ai_model_lifecycle only when at least one key reports it retired and no key can still call it; the successor Google names in the error is adopted only after it answers, and a non-text successor (tts, image, embedding, audio, live) is never adopted. Every Gemini call and the guidance value batch read that record (cached a minute), swap each retired model for its adopted successor, following successors onward, drop one with none, and never empty a chain. A probe that is neither success nor retirement (quota, billing, network) leaves the record unchanged, a retired model that answers again is restored, and with no ready key the check writes nothing. Each new retirement, changed successor or restoration notifies every super_admin (ai_key_alert); an unchanged record never re-alerts. Admin tooling — no mobile counterpart.

features.name: Free public tools — guidance value finder and property process guides on the marketing site

invariants.rule: The public guidance value finder answers a typed schedule from the imported notifications with no sign-in: POST /api/public/guidance-value/lookup requires an area, layout, village or city, is rate-limited per IP and globally before any search, never reads a file (a multipart body is refused with SIGN_IN_REQUIRED), never calls Gemini and never burns credits. Reading a sale deed schedule stays behind sign-in on /api/guidance-value/lookup under GVL-001.

Every liaison workflow template is published as a process guide at /tools/property-process/<slug>, with its stages, total days, authorities and generated questions derived from the template rather than written twice, and the hub, each tool and each guide is in the sitemap. Tool pages carry FAQ and breadcrumb structured data, process guides add HowTo with one step per stage, and the guidance value finder adds a free WebApplication served for Karnataka.

The landing page and its lead bot know the free tools: the marketing config lists Guidance Value Finder and Liaisons & Process Tracking as features with FAQs that point at the tool URLs, and the site Q&A context names every public tool by URL so the bot never denies they exist.

The public stamp duty calculator at /tools/stamp-duty charges Karnataka stamp duty on the higher of the sale price and the guidance value, applies the slab rate to the whole chargeable value, adds the surcharge for the chosen area type and the cess as percentages of the duty and the registration fee as a percentage of the chargeable value, and every rate it uses is read from one table in src/lib/tools/stamp-duty.ts that the page prints in full. An empty or negative value yields zero, never a negative charge.

The public EMI calculator at /tools/emi-calculator computes the standard reducing-balance instalment from the loan (property price less the down payment share), annual rate and tenure, amortises it year by year until the balance is zero with the principal paid summing to the loan, treats a zero rate as straight-line repayment, caps the tenure at thirty years, and reads amounts written as lakh or crore.

The public rental yield calculator at /tools/rental-yield computes gross yield as a year of rent over the price and net yield as rent less vacancy and yearly costs over the price plus one-time purchase costs, treats missing costs as zero, clamps vacancy to twelve months, reports no payback when the net income is not positive, never divides by an empty price, and inverts the price and a target yield to the monthly rent it needs.

features.name: e-Khata reading — fill a listing from its Karnataka e-Khata

invariants.rule: An e-Khata (PDF or photo, up to 10 MB) uploaded to the account's property-documents folder is read by POST /api/properties/e-khata for the listing_parse credit price, burned before the read and refunded when the read fails or the file is not an e-Khata. Only fields that validate survive: a 6-20 digit ePID, Form A or B, coordinates inside India (swapped when the form prints longitude first), feet dimensions, positive areas, construction years no later than next year, and owner names with every token carrying a digit (Aadhaar, PAN, masked IDs) stripped. A construction year is never proposed for a plot.

Reading proposes and never writes listing fields: the web form and the mobile editor show every proposed change (address, city, map pin, site area, dimensions, built-up area, year built, ePID, khata form) with values that would replace something already entered unticked, skip values that already match, never offer land fields on an apartment or built-up area on a plot, and list owner, tax, liabilities, boundaries and document number for reference only. Nothing is saved until the agent saves the listing.
A file named or captioned as an e-Khata (e-Khata, e-Khatha, Khata, ePID) is recognised as one, and a brochure, sale deed or floor plan is not.

properties.khata_epid (6-20 digits), khata_form ('A' or 'B') and year_built (1800-2100) are editable on web and mobile and normalised by both property routes, so an invalid value is cleared rather than stored. The read e-Khata is kept with the listing: the web form adds it to the document list, and the mobile editor has the server attach it to the listing's documents, and a read whose file cannot be attached fails and is refunded rather than reporting success.

A PDF forwarded to the ConvoReal WhatsApp number whose file name or caption names an e-Khata is read as one, for the same listing_parse credit as any listing: opening a draft, its address, city, map pin, site area, dimensions, built-up area, year built, ePID and khata form win over the generic read of the same file (a title is only supplied, never replaced); sent into a draft already under way, it only fills fields the draft is missing and a failed read is refunded while the file is still attached. No photo is ever extracted from an e-Khata (it carries the owner's photograph), the owner's name never becomes a contact (an owner the generic read found on the e-Khata is cleared when it opens a draft), an apartment never takes the plot's site area or dimensions and a plot never takes built-up area or year built, the khata fields survive a concurrent draft merge, and the draft preview shows the khata form, ePID and year built. The confirmed listing stores khata_epid, khata_form and year_built.

features.name: Showcase Pulse — visitor activity on shared showcase links

invariants.rule: The visitor activity feed on web and mobile loads newest-first in keyset pages ordered by created_at then id, offers Load older activity until a short page arrives, and never stops at a fixed row window, so one busy visitor cannot hide earlier days of activity.

Tapping an identified visitor in the activity feed opens that contact's details — the contact screen on mobile, the contact page from the visitor's name on web (the web avatar still opens their chat) — and an anonymous guest has no link.

A personalized showcase link belongs to the first device that opens it; any other device opening the same link is recorded as a guest via that contact's link, never as the contact, until the visitor identifies themselves, and a known device stays attributed when it returns on the bare link. The activity feed labels a forwarded-link guest by the sender's name on web and mobile.

The viewed listings panel on web and mobile lists every property with at least one showcase view, most viewed first, up to the shared 500-listing bound, inside its own scroller with the listing count in its heading; each listing still opens its viewers.

The viewed listings panel on web and mobile can be sorted by most views, fewest views, latest viewed or earliest viewed; the database applies the order before the listing bound, and every listing shows when it was last viewed.

An identified showcase visitor (contact_id set, with a phone) whose view_property dwell on one Available listing totals at least 30 seconds within the last 24 hours gets one WhatsApp check-in for that listing, sent only after their showcase activity has been quiet for 30 minutes (checked again under the send lease, which releases the claim if they are browsing again), with each view counted for at most 30 minutes because the public beacon is not trusted to cap it, and outside the account's client quiet hours. Nobody is asked twice about a listing, a contact gets at most one check-in in any 3 days, and none goes to a contact who is dead, archived, chain-only, declined alerts, inside a pitch-quiet window, classified Agent or Developer, the listing's owner (all checked again under the send lease), who wrote in or was written to by an agent since the view (checked again under the send lease), or whose share-feedback request for the listing was sent in the last 3 days or is due. While the 24-hour window is open it goes as free-form buttons naming the listing (Book a visit / Call me back / Not for me); otherwise as an approved template whose quick replies carry the same reply ids: the showcase_view_followup template (name, brokerage, listing; no opt-out footer), auto-submitted once per account as Utility and never resubmitted, ahead of the earlier showcase_view_checkin template, and a Utility row ahead of a Marketing one whatever its name, choosing among rows in the contact's language first (CLG-001); while no usable template exists the claim is released rather than skipped, so the visitor is still asked once it is approved. A Marketing-categorised template goes only to contacts who granted alerts. Each check-in is claimed before sending, a claim whose contact conversation is busy with another send is released rather than spent, its WhatsApp message id is stored, and marking it sent is retried so a delivered check-in is not sent again.

Book a visit and Call me back on a showcase check-in are acknowledged to the buyer naming the listing, recorded on the check-in and as interest on listing_feedback, and put on the assigned agent (the contact's assigned agent, else the listing's manager, else the WhatsApp owner) as a high-priority to-do (call back due within the hour, visit within three hours) and an alert under the Viewer asks for a visit or call notification setting, whose WhatsApp ping is reply-bridged to the buyer's thread. The answer is recorded on the check-in only after its to-do is written, and every visit or call-back tap, repeated or not, rewrites the interest verdict (Not for me once the listing-feedback handler has taken the tap; a repeated Not for me tap is handed over again, so a reason list that failed to send is sent on the next tap), so a tap whose to-do failed is handled in full again when the buyer taps again; tapping the same button again after its answer is recorded is acknowledged again without a second to-do or alert, while a different button (Book a visit after Call me back) is a new request and handled in full. When the acknowledgement to the buyer fails, the to-do and alert still go out and the alert tells the agent to reach the buyer directly. Not for me goes to the listing-feedback reason list and alerts nobody. A Book a visit or Call me back tap on a listing that is no longer Available gets the listing's unavailable-status reply (or, for Pending Review, a plain not-open-yet note) instead, with no to-do, alert or promise of a visit or call (PRP-014). A tap naming a listing outside the account does nothing.

The agent is alerted when an identified showcase visitor is hot on one Available listing: at least 2 minutes of total view_property dwell, or views on at least 2 separate IST days, within the last 7 days, with a view in the last 24 hours and the visitor's showcase activity quiet for 10 minutes. The alert names the contact, their phone, the listing and both signals, goes to the contact's assigned agent (else the listing's manager, else the WhatsApp owner) under the Hot viewer on a listing notification setting with WhatsApp and push held through the agent's quiet hours, and opens the contact's conversation, or the contact when there is none. A contact x listing alerts at most once a week and a contact at most once a day; dead, archived and chain-only contacts, Agent and Developer contacts, and the listing's owner never raise one, and a listing that stopped being Available by the time its claim is processed, or a contact who has since become one of the excluded kinds, or a contact or listing that cannot be read then, or a visitor who is browsing the showcase again by then, raises none and releases the claim. Each alert is claimed before it is sent.

features.name: Copilot — the in-app AI helper

invariants.rule: The floating AI helper button can be dragged anywhere on web and mobile without opening the helper, snaps to the nearer side edge, stays clear of the header and tab bar, remembers its position on the device, and still opens the helper on a plain tap.

The floating AI Assistant launcher and the Help & feedback control never overlap: the launcher collapses to an icon once the main content scrolls, and a dragged launcher is clamped to rest at least 64px from the bottom, above the Help control.

A staff question asking which contacts are looking for an area, property type, BHK or budget is answered from the account's own contact rows: a bounded list of matching contacts, each a link that opens that contact's card on web and mobile, plus a link to the filtered Contacts list, with no phone numbers in the answer, no tour offered in its place, and never served from or stored in the shared answer cache.

features.name: Seller page — a seller's live listings on the agency's showcase

invariants.rule: A seller page lists only published listings whose owner is the seller and whose listing source is not agent-referred; with none live it renders its own empty state and never the agency's full catalogue or its listing links.
Every call and WhatsApp prompt on a seller page uses the agency's own number, and the seller's contact id, name and phone never reach the page; the browser identifies the page only by its slug.
Creating a new link or turning a seller page off makes the previous URL answer with HTTP 404 on the next request.
A seller slug opened on a tenant host that belongs to a different account answers with HTTP 404 rather than that account's catalogue.

Showcase events from a seller page credit guests to the seller through via_contact_id and flag the page open, and enquiries and requirements from it record the seller as referrer; a slug from another account is ignored.

Only agent-role members can turn a seller page on, rotate it or turn it off, from the contact record on web and mobile alike; Portfolio on web and mobile shows each linked agency's live link, or asks the seller to request one.

features.name: Account membership and roles

invariants.rule: A member's account, role and read-only status change only through the member RPCs (set_member_role, set_member_org_role, set_member_team, transfer_account_ownership, remove_account_member, redeem_invitation) and server-side setup; a signed-in client cannot insert a profile row, and updating its own row cannot change account_id, account_role, org_role, is_read_only, team_id or the platform role column, so no role-, team- or platform-admin-gated check can be cleared by self-edit or by a persona without a profile (Portfolio owner or buyer) creating one, and the profile-setup route bootstraps a brokerage account only through bootstrap_staff_account, a service-role-only database function that holds a per-user lock before it looks for a profile, so overlapping calls return the one account instead of minting an orphan tenant; redeems a live team invitation under a row lock by marking it accepted and attaching the user to the inviting account with the invited role, never creating an account for it; re-runs the sign-up invite gate under row locks for a new tenant (a live beta invitation while the gate is on, one seat per invitation); and never runs for a Portfolio owner or buyer identity.

A read-only member (profiles.is_read_only, stored as an agent-level org_agent) cannot create, change, run or delete automations or flows, nor activate or buy a marketplace flow. Every mutating route for them (POST /api/automations, PATCH and DELETE /api/automations/[id], POST /api/automations/[id]/duplicate, POST /api/automations/engine, POST /api/flows, PUT and DELETE /api/flows/[id], POST /api/flows/[id]/activate, POST /api/marketplace/items/[id]/activate and /checkout, the last two tested together in the activate route test) uses requireWriteRole('agent') and answers 403 before writing, while their GET routes stay open to read-only members. The database refuses the same writes on its own: the write policies on flows, flow_nodes, automations and automation_steps use is_account_writer(), which is is_account_member() plus the read-only check, so a read-only member's own JWT cannot write them through PostgREST either. The web UI matches with useCan('make-changes') (canSendMessages && !isReadOnly): create, edit, delete and activate actions are hidden or disabled, and the flow editor opens read-only with every mutation a no-op and no media upload, while node disclosures and canvas navigation stay usable.

Row-level security refuses a read-only member (profiles.is_read_only) on every workspace write, at every role level, so their own JWT cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE through PostgREST whatever an API route allows. Every write policy uses is_account_writer() (is_account_member() plus the read-only check) or names is_read_only itself; a new migration that adds a write policy on is_account_member() alone fails the test. A read-only member keeps every read they had: where a tightened FOR ALL policy was a table's only read path (contact_property_inquiries, portal_accounts, portal_import_items) a separate SELECT policy keeps it. They may still write only rows that are their own or are not a workspace change: their profile, notification devices, notification read state, task-digest preference (agent_task_digest_settings), a support ticket and a bug report. Members who are not read-only are unaffected. The storage write policies on the property-images, property-images-private and property-documents buckets follow the same rule: each requires is_account_writer() on the account id that is the object's first folder, so a read-only member cannot upload, replace or delete listing media, and nobody can write a property document under an account they cannot write to.

A SECURITY DEFINER function that writes without checking who called it is never reachable over PostgREST RPC. _bcast_bump, bump_copilot_qa_hit, vote_copilot_qa, log_copilot_unmet_request, sync_contact_budget_band, seed_default_reminder_templates, claim_broadcast_dispatch, release_broadcast_dispatch, renew_broadcast_dispatch, renew_broadcast_recipient_claims, claim_broadcast_recipients and recompute_broadcast_counts take a row or account id and write to it with no membership check, so EXECUTE on each is revoked from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated and granted to service_role alone: a signed-out visitor or a member of another account calling one with their own key is refused by the database before the body runs. Their only callers keep working: the broadcast dispatcher and the Copilot answer cache and demand log call them through the service-role client (supabaseAdmin), and the broadcast-count, budget-band and default-template triggers reach theirs from SECURITY DEFINER trigger functions that run as the function owner. A new SECURITY DEFINER function that writes either guards its account with is_account_writer() when a member calls it with their own JWT, or revokes EXECUTE from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated when only server code and triggers call it; granting service_role alone in the migration is not enough, because a new function in public is executable by every role until it is revoked.

A read-only member cannot write through a SECURITY DEFINER function either. Row-level security does not apply inside one, so each function that writes on behalf of the calling member guards with is_account_writer() rather than is_account_member(): allocate_invoice_number, deal_invoice_append, deal_invoice_remove, issue_invoice, journey_show_captured, sync_listing_status_from_deals, unmap_portal_ad and bulk_tag_properties at agent level, resync_pipeline_stage_deals, revoke_beta_invite and rotate_beta_invite at admin level. A read-only member calling one over PostgREST with their own JWT is refused the way a non-member is. sync_listing_status_from_deals keeps its service-role branch, so server code and triggers running as the service role still sync a listing. complete_copilot_appointment refuses read-only members with its own profile check and stays as it is. A new SECURITY DEFINER function that inserts, updates or deletes for the caller uses is_account_writer(); is_account_member() is for reads.

A read-only member (profiles.is_read_only, stored as an agent-level org_agent) cannot hand a contact off to another agent or issue a beta invitation. POST /api/contacts/[id]/handoff and POST /api/beta-invites use requireWriteRole('agent') and answer 403 before calling the database. The two SECURITY DEFINER functions behind them refuse on their own, so the member's own JWT cannot run them through PostgREST RPC either: handoff_contact and issue_beta_invite check is_account_writer(<caller's account>, 'agent') right after resolving the caller's profile and raise 42501 before the contact is reassigned or the seat is inserted. Every other check in the two functions (same-account contact and target, the org-role handoff rules, the open beta programme and the per-account quota) is unchanged.

A read-only member (profiles.is_read_only) cannot manage the team, whatever account_role or org_role they hold. PATCH and DELETE /api/account/members/[userId] use requireWriteRole('admin'), POST /api/account/transfer-ownership uses requireWriteRole('owner'), PATCH /api/account/members/[userId]/org-role and /team refuse ctx.isReadOnly after their org-role check, and DELETE /api/account/delete refuses a read-only owner before relocating teammates; each answers 403 before calling the database. The SECURITY DEFINER functions behind them refuse on their own, so the member's own JWT cannot run them through PostgREST RPC either: set_member_role, set_member_org_role, set_member_team, remove_account_member and transfer_account_ownership check is_account_writer(<caller's account>, 'agent') right after resolving the caller's profile and raise 42501 before any write. Every other check in them (role thresholds, same-account target, the owner and Manager carve-outs, the Leader team rules) is unchanged. mark_bot_instructions_fired, which already did nothing unless auth.role() is service_role, is executable by service_role only.

features.name: AI credits wallet and transaction history

invariants.rule: The credits history names what each row was for, never the marker the ledger stores: a refund reads "Refund — <feature>" and a charge reads the feature's name, whether its description is a refund marker (refund:<burn id>), a retry key (retry:<key>) or "<feature> burn", while a description a person wrote is kept as written. Web (including its CSV export) and mobile render the one label from the same function, so the two surfaces cannot disagree about it.

A voice call attempt, a reminder call and a listing video render are refunded by the charge each one made, never by feature and amount: a dial is charged and refunded under voice-call:<recipient>:<attempt>, shared by the dispatcher's start-failure and stale-requeue refunds and the post-call webhook's no-answer refund; a reminder call is refunded under its own retry key; and a listing video's burn key travels in the queued job, with a job queued before keys existed still refunded by amount. Each refund goes through refundBurn, so it reverses at most the rows written under that key and is queued for the hourly credit-refunds cron if the call fails.

The AI routes named in keyed-refund-routes.test.ts (ad copy, photo enhancement, listing descriptions, greetings, event parsing, share email, call analysis and call action items, deal document reads, guidance value lookups and e-Khata reads) charge credits before their call and return them when it fails by the charge they made: the route mints one burn key per request, burns under it, and every failure path refunds that key through refundBurn, so a refund reverses at most the rows written under that key and a refund that fails is queued for the hourly credit-refunds cron instead of failing the route. What the route then tells the user follows the refund's outcome, and never says credits were refunded unless they were.

A reminder voice note and a reminder call are each charged under a key that names one charge, never the subject: a reminder voice note under a key minted for each run of the worker (reminder_audio:<uuid>), so a replayed job or a claim taken over after a lost send never shares a charge with an earlier run, and a reminder call under a key minted for the call (voice_campaign_call:<uuid>), so a re-armed or taken-over reminder never shares a charge with an earlier call. Each failure refunds that key through refundBurn, which reverses only the rows written under it, and neither feature is refunded by feature and amount. A match unlock is not covered: it still refunds by feature and amount until its charge and the unlock row are written atomically.

An audio announcement is charged under its own burn key, stored on its row (voice_announcements.burn_key), and refunded by that key through refundBurn on every failure. A render that fails in the worker refunds that key. A row whose insert fails, or a job that cannot be queued, is first cancelled by the charge's key, only while the row is still generating and retrying the update, so a row the insert committed before its reply was lost is cancelled too, a row that does not exist counts as cancelled, and a cancellation whose own reply was lost is recognised by the row's failed status and error; the refund follows only a confirmed cancellation. When the cancellation cannot be made at all the refund is held and the charge's key is logged for manual reconciliation, because the job may have been queued after all. The worker ignores a row that is no longer generating and marks a row ready only while it is, so a push that was committed after all cannot render an announcement whose credits were refunded. A row created before keys existed has no burn_key and is still refunded by feature and amount.

features.name: Match Radar — one-tap WhatsApp alerts for matched buyers and listings

invariants.rule: A Match Radar event's alerts reach each recipient once, enforced by the server rather than the client. POST /api/radar/send claims the event with one conditional update before it sends anything; while that claim is live (6 minutes, longer than the route can run) another send of the same event is refused with 409 SEND_IN_PROGRESS and sends nothing. Each recipient is recorded on the event before its alert goes out and taken off again only when that send is known not to have reached Meta (refused before or by Meta); a failure after Meta accepted any part of the alert, or a request whose outcome is unknown, keeps the recipient recorded, so a run that dies mid-send can never be retried into a duplicate, and every later send of the event skips recorded recipients: a resubmit from a stale screen or a retry after a crashed batch reaches only recipients who do not have the alert yet, and is refused with 409 ALREADY_SENT when every selected recipient already has it (as is an event sent before recipients were recorded). Only the re-engagement Send again button, which asks to resend, delivers to a recipient twice. A send that delivered nothing releases the claim so the card can be retried, one that delivered anything marks the event sent, even when a later target threw, and sent_count adds to the total current when the claim was taken. Web and mobile show the refusal ("This alert is already being sent." / "This alert was already sent.") from one shared mapping and refresh the feed instead of resending.

features.name: Buyer conversations — what a lead hears from the bot, read as one thread

invariants.rule: A portal lead whose enquired listing has left the market is greeted by one message, the listing status notice (free-form inside an open window, the approved Utility template outside it), never the welcome auto-reply beside it; the welcome goes out only when no notice is sent. The notice names the listing once, without repeating a locality its title already carries and without the title's trailing punctuation, and the free-form reply ends with the lead's attributed showcase link. The exact-matched listing's own locality, type and price are recorded on the lead beside the portal's wording of them.

A lead who taps Update my preferences is shown live listings before being told nothing fits: the 5 km strict search runs first and the ordinary 20 km search only when it is empty; a budget inferred from the enquired listing's price (pref_budget_anchor) admits listings up to 15% above it as partial fits while a stated budget keeps the 10% rule; a stated area that is a phase or block of a known locality takes that locality's coordinates for the radius. The reply greets a lead created within the last week as answering their own enquiry and only an older lead as back on our radar, never praises the matching engine, names the near-miss stock in the lead's own locality when nothing fits, carries the lead's attributed showcase link, and ends on the one qualifying question.

The on-demand matches reply (MATCHES, Show Properties) never answers a dead end bare: when the enquired listing is unavailable and nothing fits it names that listing once (without its trailing punctuation), the near-miss stock in the lead's locality, the lead's attributed showcase link, then the widening question; when the thread's recent bot messages already told the lead the listing is unavailable (a status notice template or an earlier reply) it does not say so again; every no-match reply ends with the showcase link ahead of its question.

A portal lead on an unavailable listing is replayed end to end through the real lead-arrival replies, the Update my preferences and Show Properties steps, the matcher, the near-miss search and the showcase links against an in-memory inventory, and the whole thread passes the transcript rules: one arrival bubble naming the listing once, at most two bot bubbles per customer turn, the live listing two phases over shown before any no-match wording, and on a true dead end the locality's stock at another price (a phase or block searched as its parent locality too) plus the showcase link. The on-demand brief names a bare sector with its noun and an enquiry-anchored budget as around, never up to.

The transcript rules read a bot thread the way the lead did and are the one definition of a bad thread for the replay harness, the pinned fixtures and the nightly review: no more than two bot bubbles per customer turn, no arrival that promises listings and withdraws the listing in the next bubble, the listing's unavailability stated at most once, no free-form dead end without a link, no praise of the engine, no welcome-back copy for a lead created within the week, and a Show Properties tap answered with a listing or a link. Every real thread pinned under transcripts/fixtures declares exactly the violations the rules report for it, so a rule that stops catching a recorded incident fails the build; fixtures carry no phone number or email.

Every conversation the bot wrote in during the last day is reviewed nightly (05:00 IST) as one thread: the transcript rules run first, then the model judge scores it with the lead's numbers and emails masked, and one bot_thread_reviews row per conversation per IST day records the transcript, the violations, the score, the issues and a verdict that fails on any rule violation or a score under 70, is unscored only when the rules pass and the judge gave no score, and is never recomputed on a rerun; a run that dies mid-judge leaves a claim the next night takes over, and a judge that throws releases its claim so the thread is retried rather than recorded unscored. Platform admins see failed and unscored threads on Admin → Bot replies with the issues beside the bubbles, record their own good or bad verdict, and copy a thread out as a fixture whose expected violations are the ones the rules found.
